dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text: Hello! Today we are learning our Unit 1 words — the words for school things, colours, people and actions. We learn them by hearing them, saying them out loud, and using them in our own sentences. By the end you will be able to say each word, tell me what it means, and write it in a sentence. You need your voice, your eyes, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. Let's begin! 1. Look at the word list on the left side. Press one word. A card will open for that word. There are 67 words, and we do one word at a time. Start with the very first one. 2. Press Hear it. Listen carefully. Now say the word out loud — a big brave voice, not a quiet head voice. Then press Again and say it one more time. I expect to hear your voice both times. 3. Now read the Meaning on the card. Press the little speaker next to it to hear it read to you. Then say the meaning in your own words, out loud. It does not have to be perfect — just tell me what the word means to you. 4. Look at In a sentence. Read each sentence, then press Hear sentence to listen to it. Use the arrows to see every sentence for that word. Then pick one sentence and read it out loud yourself. Nice and slow. 5. Look at the Spelling line on the card. Say the letters one by one, like this: b... o... o... k. Then say the whole word again. This helps your eyes remember the word. 6. Now go to Write your own sentence. Type a sentence with the word in the box. The grey words are there to help you start. Press Check sentence, read what it tells you, and fix anything it says. I expect one sentence that makes sense and uses your word. 7. When you can say the word, tell its meaning, and you have written your sentence, press I know this word. The word will get a LEARNED tag in the list. That means you did it! 8. Now press the next word in the list. Do all the same steps again: Hear it, Again, Meaning, In a sentence, Spelling, Write your own sentence, then I know this word. One word at a time. Take your time — there's no rush. 9. Under the word list there is a deck of slides with the same words, one word on each slide. Press Start on the first slide, called Say the words. On each slide press Hear it and Again, press Meaning, read the sentences and press Hear sentence, look at the Spelling line, open Write your own sentence and press Check sentence, then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right for the next slide — the little dots show you where you are. On the last slide, when every word is marked, press the finish button. The cards at the top and the slides at the bottom teach the same words, so you can choose either one. You will know the page is finished when every word in the list has a LEARNED tag next to it, and no word is left plain. Then you can tell your grown-up: "I learned all my words!" Great work today!

overview.label: Overview
overview.text:
Hello! I am your teacher today, and I am so glad you are here. This page is called Overview. Overview means "a first look". It shows you what our new unit is about: Welcome to School. We are doing it so you know what is coming, just like looking at a map before a trip. By the end you will know what you will learn, and how to work through each page. You need your eyes, your ears, and your voice. Your grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. There are three small steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Read the unit preview on this page. It is the little bit of writing that tells you what you will learn. If you see a Listen button, press it and follow the words with your finger as you hear them. I expect you to look and listen all the way to the end, and then say out loud one thing you will learn. For example: "I will learn colours!"

Step 2. Read the four steps under How to learn. These four steps tell you how we work on every page of this unit. Read them slowly, one at a time. I expect you to try saying step one back to me in your own words. Even a few words is great. Step 3. Now press the button that says I have previewed this unit. That tells the page you have had your first look. Then press Open vocabulary. That takes you to our first learning page, where we meet our new words. I expect you to press them in that order: first I have previewed this unit, then Open vocabulary. You will know this page is finished when you have listened to the preview, read the four How to learn steps, and pressed both buttons. Then our new page opens and our words are waiting! Ready? Start with Step 1, and tell me one thing you will learn in this unit. 😊

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text:
Hello! I am so happy you are here. 🌟

This page is our video lesson for Unit 1, "Welcome to School". You will watch a teacher on the screen. They will show you school words like table, chair, book and pencil, and colour words like red and blue. Watching and listening is how the words go into your ears first. Then saying them out loud puts the words in your mouth too! Here is what you need: a quiet spot, your ears ready, and your voice ready. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. There are three steps. Here they all are. 1. Press play on the video and watch it all the way to the end. Sit comfortably and look at the screen. Words will appear at the bottom — those are the captions. Try to look at them while you listen. I expect you to watch the whole video without stopping, right to the last part. If you miss something, that is okay — you can play it again. 2. Say the words out loud with the teacher in the video. When the teacher says "table", you say "table" too. When the teacher says "This is a book", you say it back. Say it clearly, not in a tiny whisper. I expect you to join in with your voice, not just watch quietly. Copy the teacher's mouth and try to make your word sound the same. Say it with me, slowly. 3. When the video has finished, press the button under it to go on to Vocabulary. Only press it after the video is really over. That button takes you to the next part of our unit, where we look at the words closely. I expect you to finish the video first, then press it. You will know this page is finished when the video has played to the very end, you have said the words out loud with the teacher, and you have pressed the button to go to Vocabulary. Off you go — press play! When you come back, tell me one new word you heard. 😊

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text:
Hello! Today I am your reading teacher. 📚

This page is our reading shelf. It has three texts: the story "Amal's First Day", a talking page called "Talk about Welcome to School", and the "Hello, School!" rhyme. We read them so school words like table, chair, book and crayon get easy for you. By the end you will read them all and say some words out loud. You need your eyes, your finger, and your brave voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is near. There are 6 steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Read the text on your screen slowly. Point at each word with your finger as you go. Read it out loud if you can — even a whisper counts. I expect you to go slowly, not fast. Slow reading is good reading. Step 2. Press Prepare audio. Wait a moment. Then press the play button. Now listen and follow the words with your finger. I expect your finger to move with the voice. If you lose your place, press play again and start over. That is fine. Step 3. If a text is a listening text, listen first, then read along with the voice. One of these three texts is our unit story, "Amal's First Day". That is the one our questions are about, so read that one extra carefully. I expect you to remember two things from the story — maybe a name, or a colour. Step 4. Press Next text to go to the next one. Press Previous text to go back. Read every text on the shelf, all three. I expect you to try each one, even the rhyme. Say the rhyme out loud — it is fun to say a bit louder each time. Step 5. Now look under the reading. There is a deck of slides with the same text, one small page at a time. On the first slide, press Start. On each page, read the words, or press the speaker to listen. Then press the arrow to turn the page. On the last page, press I have read this text. I expect you to read every slide, not skip ahead. Step 6. When you have read all the texts and finished the slides, press Finished reading. You will know the page is done when you have pressed I have read this text on the slides, and Finished reading at the end. 🌟

Off you go with Step 1 — take your time, there's no rush. Tell me when it is done, and I will be right here.

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Comprehension page. 📚

Comprehension means showing that you understand the story. We read about Amal's first day at school, and now we tell what happened. This helps you remember the story and say good English sentences. You need the story on the page, your reading eyes, and your speaking voice. A grown-up can sit with you and read the questions out loud. Here is what I expect from you today. Try every question. Answer in a full sentence, not just one word. And it is fine to look back at the story — good readers do that! There are 5 steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Look at the questions. There are 12 questions about the texts you read. Read one question at a time. Ask yourself, what is this question really asking? Then think about the story part that tells you. If you cannot remember, read that bit of the story again. I expect you to think first, before you type. Step 2. Type your answer in the box. Write a full sentence, not just one word. For example, if the question asks who smiled at Amal, do not write only a name. Write it like this: The boy who smiled at Amal is ___. Start with a big letter and end with a full stop. I expect one whole sentence in the box for each question. Step 3. Press Check guidance. This shows you a good answer, so you can compare it with yours. If your box is empty, the page will ask you to write first, so always type before you press. Do this for every one of the 12 questions. If your answer is different, that is okay — look for the same idea, not the same words. Step 4. Do the slides at the bottom. Under the questions there is a deck called Think about the story, with one question on each slide. Press Start. Say your answer out loud in a big, clear voice. Then press Check guidance to see a good answer. Press the arrow to go to the next question. On the last slide, press Finish comprehension. I expect you to speak, not just think — your voice is doing the learning here. Step 5. Press Finish comprehension at the bottom of the page. Do this only when you have answered all 12 questions and finished the slides. This is you telling the page, I am done! You will know the page is finished when every question box has your sentence in it, you have pressed Check guidance on each one, the slides are all done, and you have pressed Finish comprehension at the bottom. Ready? Start with question one, and tell me when you have typed your first answer. Take your time — there's no rush.

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text:
Hello! I am your teacher today. 🌟

This page is called Grammar. Grammar means the way we put words together to make a good sentence. On this page you will learn six little sentence patterns, like "This is a book" and "I like apples". By the end, you will be able to say your name, your age, and tell people about school things. You need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. Let's start! Step 1. Look at the six grammar lessons on the page. Start with the first one. Read the rule and the examples, then press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear it read to you. Listen carefully all the way to the end. I expect you to listen first, before you talk. Do this for one lesson at a time. Step 2. Now say the examples out loud. Say them with a big, brave voice — not a whisper. Say each one twice: once slowly, once a bit faster. I expect to hear the whole sentence, like "This is a pencil," not just "pencil."

Step 3. Under the lesson, press Show practice. Try the practice sentences yourself. Then press Hear the practice to check how they sound. If your words sound the same, well done! If not, say it again with the audio. Do this for every one of the six lessons, one by one. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 4. Go down to the slides at the bottom. This part is called Say the patterns. Press Start. On each slide there is one pattern. Say the pattern out loud, try the practice, then press the speaker to hear it. Then move to the next slide. I expect you to go through every slide, right to the last one. Do not skip any! Step 5. When all six lessons and all the slides are done, press the button that says I practised all the lessons. That button is at the bottom of the page. Only press it when you really have done them all — you are being honest and brave. How will you know the page is finished? When you have heard all six lessons, said all the examples out loud, done every practice, reached the last slide, and pressed I practised all the lessons. 🎉

Here is one small tip from me: in English we say "I am six years old," not "I have six years." And we say "I can write," not "I can to write."

Go and start with lesson one now. Come back and tell me when it is done, and I will check it with you. Take your time — there's no rush.

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text:
Hello! Today we are doing our Speaking page together. Speaking is where we say English out loud with our own voice. This page has six little practices, like "This is a pencil" and "My name is ___." By the end you will be able to say all six sentences clearly and proudly. You need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby if one can sit with you. Here is our whole plan. There are six steps. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 1. Listen and say. In each practice, press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear the model sentence. Listen two times. Then say the same sentence out loud yourself, nice and clear. I expect a big brave voice, not a whisper. Say it with me, slowly. Step 2. Record. Press the microphone button. Say your sentence. Then press the microphone again to stop. I expect one whole sentence, like "This is a pencil," not just one word. Step 3. Listen. Play your recording back and listen to yourself. Ask yourself one question: can I hear every word? This is how good speakers check their work. Step 4. Submit. After you listen back, the Submit for pronunciation check button turns on. Press it. Read what the checker tells you, or ask your grown-up to read it. If you want to do better, record again. Do this for every one of the six practices. Step 5. The slides at the bottom. Under the practices there is a deck called Use your voice, with one practice on each slide. Press Start. Press Hear model. Say it yourself. Press Record, then press Submit. Then press the arrow to go to the next practice. Keep going until the slides are done. Step 6. Finish. When all the practices are done, press the Finish speaking practices button at the bottom of the page. You will know the page is finished when every practice has your recording and a check, the slides are all done, and you have pressed Finish speaking practices. Then the page is complete. 🌟

Now start with Step 1. When you have said your first sentence out loud, tell me which sentence you said, and I will tell you what to do next.

writing.label: Writing
writing.text: Hello! I am your teacher today. This page is our Writing page. Here you draw, trace and write tiny sentences about school. We do it because writing helps you show your ideas to other people. By the end, you will be able to write short school sentences like "This is a chair" and "I like my book." You need a pencil, some paper, and your best try. A grown-up can sit with you and help you read. Here is what I expect: say your sentence out loud first, then write it. Neat is nice, but brave is better. Wobbly letters are completely fine in Grade 1. 1. There are 6 writing tasks. Look at the list and press the first task to open it. Press Hear the task if you see a little speaker, and listen carefully. Our six tasks are: Draw and tell, Trace, Match and copy, Label, Complete a pattern, and Create one sentence. I expect you to start with task 1 and go in order. 2. Press View model text. This shows you an example of good writing, like "This is a chair." Read it out loud, or ask your grown-up to read it with you. Do not copy it word for word. I expect you to look at how it starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. 3. Now write your own in the big box. Use the sentence starter for that task: This is a ___ , It is ___ , My name is ___ , I am ___ years old , I can ___ , I like ___ . Try to make about eight words in total — you can write two short sentences to get there, like "This is a book. I like my book." Use the Writer's checklist to check your work. Press Support if you feel stuck, and press Challenge if you want a bigger job. I expect a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end. 4. When you are happy, press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved, so you can come back and make it better any time. Then go back to the list and do the next task, one after another, until all six are done. 5. Look under the tasks. There is a slide deck called Plan, write and improve, with one task on each slide. Press Start, say your sentence out loud, then write it in the box — again about eight words. Press Submit this draft. Then press the arrow to go to the next task slide. Keep going until the last slide. You will know the page is finished when all 6 tasks show as submitted and you have pressed the arrow through every slide. Now go and do step 1. Tell me which task you chose, and I will help you with it!

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text:
Hello! I am your teacher today. This page is our Welcome to School checkpoint. It is a little quiz with ten questions about our unit: classroom things, colours, and our talking sentences like "My name is ___."

We do this to see what you have learned. It is not scary. It is a happy way to show what you know. You need your eyes, your thinking brain, and a grown-up nearby if you want one. Here is what I expect from you: try every question yourself. I will not tell you answers, but I will help you think. Take your time — there's no rush. Here are the steps. 1. Start question one. Read the question slowly, twice. Look at all the answer choices before you pick. Then click the one answer you think is right. Some questions ask "which thing is in a classroom?" — so picture our classroom in your head. Some ask "which sentence tells your name?" — so look for the words "My name is". Some ask about sounds — so say each word out loud and listen to the very first sound. I expect one careful choice for each question, not a fast guess. 2. Keep going, one question at a time, until all ten are done. Do not worry if one feels hard. Skip past the tricky feeling, pick your best answer, and move on. I expect you to answer all ten, even the hard ones. Brave tries count. 3. Look at your score at the end. The page will show you how many you got right. More than half right means you passed — that is six or more out of ten. I expect you to read your score and tell me how you did. 4. If your score is not high enough, press Try again. That button starts the quiz once more. Before you start, think about the words we learned: table, chair, book, pencil, clock, and our colours. Then answer all ten again, slowly. I expect a second brave try — mistakes are how we learn. 5. When your score is good, press Continue. That button takes you to My progress, where your work is saved. I expect you to press it yourself, because your work must come from you. You will know this page is finished when you have pressed Continue and you can see My progress on your screen. Ready? Go and read question one, then come back and tell me how it went. I am right here! 🌟

games.label: Games
games.text: Welcome to our Games page! Today we play games with our Unit 1 words: school things like table, chair, book and pencil, colour words like red and blue, and our talking sentences like "My name is..." and "I can...". We play because playing helps words stick in your head. What I expect from you is easy: try every game, say the words out loud, and keep going even if a game feels tricky. You need your voice, your eyes, and a grown-up nearby if you like. Here are the three steps. 1. Press a game to open it, then play it. Look at the picture or the word, take your time, and say your answer out loud before you press it. You earn stars and XP for what you know. If you get stuck, use a hint — hints are there to help you, not to trick you. If you get one wrong, press retry and try again. I expect you to say each word out loud, not just tap. 2. Play every game at least once. Do not stop after one — go back and press the next game, then the next, until you have played them all. Then play your favourite ones again to win more stars. I expect you to finish each game you open, and to try again on any game with only a few stars. 3. When you have played them all, press the button that says I have played them all. Press it only after you have really opened and played every game. I expect you to be honest here — that is part of being a good learner. You will know the page is finished when it says so: if you master every game, the page finishes all by itself, and if not, pressing I have played them all finishes it for you. Now go and press your first game. Come back and tell me which one you played and how many stars you got — I want to hear! ⭐

activities.label: Activities
activities.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this is our Activities page for Welcome to School. Here we play, colour, point and talk. We do this so the school words feel easy in your mouth: table, chair, book, pencil, red, blue, green, yellow. By the end you will be able to name school things, say colours, and say "My name is ___. I am ___ years old. I can ___."

You will need crayons, paper, a pencil, and your voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. I expect you to try every activity, say the words out loud, and not worry about neat colouring. Brave trying is the win here. Here are your steps. 1. Look at the top of the page. There are 6 activities. Read the words for activity one, then press Hear the instructions to listen to them. Listen carefully, then say back to yourself what you must do. Do this for each activity before you start it. I expect you to listen first, then begin. 2. Now do the activity. Activity 1 is colouring: the red book, the blue pencil, the green chair, the yellow door. Say each colour out loud as you colour it. Activity 2 is drawing you at school, then saying "My name is ___. I am ___ years old. This is my school." Activity 3 is colouring four circles red, blue, green and yellow, then finding a real thing in your room of each colour and naming it. Activity 4 is tracing your name, then doing three moves: stand up, sit down, put up your hand, saying each one. Activity 5 is listening for bag, pen, book and chair, pointing to the right picture, and saying "I can see a ___." Activity 6 is making a name card: fold it, write your name big, draw one thing you can do, then say "I can ___."

3. Some activities have a box. Write your answer in the box. One or two words is plenty. Say the word out loud first, then write it. Wobbly letters are fine — I only want to see letters I can read. 4. When you have finished one activity, press Mark complete under that activity. Only press it after you really did it. Then go to the next one and start again at listening. 5. Now scroll down to the slides at the bottom. This part is called Learn by doing. There is one activity on each slide. Press Start, do the activity on that slide, then press Mark complete. Press the arrow to go to the next slide. Do the same on every slide. On the last slide, press Finish activities. 6. Last of all, press Finish activities at the bottom of the whole page. Press it only when all six activities and all the slides are done. You will know the page is finished when every activity has Mark complete pressed, and you have pressed Finish activities at the bottom. That means your work is saved. Ready? Start with number one, press Hear the instructions, and tell me when you have coloured the red book. 🌟

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text: Hello! Today we are on the Books page. This is our story time. You will choose a book, look at the pictures, and hear the words in English. Books help you meet our unit words like book, chair, crayon and happy. All you need is your eyes, your ears, and your reading voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. Here is what I expect from you: try to say some words out loud, look carefully at the pictures, and go all the way to the end of your book. Take your time — there's no rush. 1. Choose a book from the shelf. Look at the shelf on your screen. Look at the covers and pick one you like. Tap the book you want. A good choice is a book that looks fun to you — there is no wrong one! I expect you to pick one book, not five. 2. Now read your book. Press the arrow to turn to the next page. If your book plays like a video, just watch and listen. Tap the pictures — they make sounds and say words! Say the words out loud with the story if you can. I expect you to look at every page, not skip ahead. 3. Keep going right to the end. When you reach the last page, press Finish book. That tells the page you did it. One book finishes this page. If you are enjoying it, you may read more books — that makes me very happy! You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Finish book on the last page of one book. Then come and tell me one thing you saw in your story!

overview.label: Overview
overview.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 2: Family Time. This page is called Overview. Overview means "a quick look at everything" — like peeking at a picture before you read the story. We do this so you know what is coming: family words, food words, and counting from one to ten. You need your eyes, your ears, and your voice. Ready? Here come three steps. 1. Read the unit preview. Look at the words at the top of this page. They tell you what you will learn in Unit 2. If you see a Listen button, press it. Then follow the words with your finger while you listen. Do it well by saying one or two words out loud with the voice — try "family" and "grandma". I expect you to listen all the way to the end, and to know one thing you will learn. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Read the four steps under How to learn. There are four little steps there. They show how you will work on every page of this unit. Read them slowly, one at a time. A grown-up can read them with you if one is near. I expect you to point at each step as you go, and to remember which step comes first. 3. Press the buttons. First press I have previewed this unit. That button tells the page, "Yes, I looked!" Then press Open vocabulary. That takes you to the first page, where we learn our new words. I expect you to press I have previewed this unit before Open vocabulary — first one, then the other. You will know this page is finished when you have listened to the preview, read the four How to learn steps, pressed I have previewed this unit, and the vocabulary page opens up. Great work today! Come back and tell me one word you saw — I would love to hear it. 😊

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 2, Family Time. This page is our video lesson. You will watch, listen and say words about your family — mum, dad, sister, brother, grandma, grandpa. Watching first helps your ears learn the sounds before your mouth tries them. All you need is your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. There are three steps. Here they all are. 1. Press play on the video and watch it right to the end. Sit somewhere comfy and quiet. Keep your eyes on the screen and look at the words at the bottom — those are the captions. Try to hear the family words when the teacher says them. I expect you to watch the whole video, not stop halfway. 2. Say the words and sentences out loud with the video. When the teacher says "grandma", you say "grandma" too. Say it in a big, brave voice — not a whisper. Try the sentences as well, like "This is my mum." Nobody is checking if it is perfect. I just expect you to open your mouth and try every time. Say it with me, slowly. 3. When the video finishes, press the button under it to go on to Vocabulary. That is the next page, where we look at the words more closely. Only press it after the video has ended, so you do not miss anything. You will know this page is finished when the video has played to the end, you have said the words out loud with the teacher, and you have pressed the button to go to Vocabulary. Then come and tell me one family word you heard. Take your time — there's no rush.

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text:
Hello! Today I am your reading teacher. 📖

This page is our reading shelf. It has three texts about Unit 2, Family Time. One is our story, "Breakfast at Grandma's House". One is a talking page called "Talk about Family Time". One is a rhyme and a counting song. We read them so we meet our family words — mum, dad, grandma, grandpa — again and again, and so our reading voice gets stronger. What I expect from you: read slowly, point with your finger, and say the words out loud if you can. A grown-up can sit with you. Take your time — there's no rush. Here are all six steps. 1. Read the text on the screen. Look at the words on the page and read them slowly, one word at a time. Read out loud if you can — even a whisper voice is good. If a word is hard, stop, look at it, and try the first sound. I expect you to read the whole text, not just the first line. 2. Listen to it too. Press Prepare audio and wait a moment. Then press the play button. Follow the words with your finger while the voice reads. I expect your finger to move along with the voice, word by word. This helps your eyes and ears work together. 3. Read the story carefully. If a text is a listening text, listen to it first, then read along with it. Our unit story is "Breakfast at Grandma's House". The Comprehension questions come from that story, so read it slowly and think about who is in it and what they eat. I expect you to know Amal, her baby brother, and the ten green grapes by the end. 4. Move to the next text. Press Next text to go forward. Press Previous text to go back if you want to read one again. Read every single one — all three. I expect no text left unread. It is fine to read your favourite one twice! 5. Do the slides at the bottom. Under the reading there is a deck of slides. It shows the same text, but one small page at a time. On the first slide, press Start (it says "Read the story"). On each page, read the words, or press the speaker to listen. Then press the arrow to turn to the next page. On the last page, press I have read this text. I expect you to read every slide, not skip to the end. 6. Finish the page. When you have read all three texts and done the slides, press Finished reading. That tells the page you are done. You will know the page is finished when you have read all three texts, pressed I have read this text on the last slide, and pressed Finished reading. Then it is done! Great work today! Come back and tell me your favourite part of the story — I would love to hear it.

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Vocabulary page of Unit 2, Family Time. This page teaches you our word list — words like mum, dad, grandma, banana, five and help. We learn them by hearing them, saying them out loud, and using them. By the end, you will be able to say each word, tell me what it means, and put it in your own sentence. You need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby if you want help reading. Say the words out loud — that is how they stick! Here are all the steps. Do them one at a time. Take your time — there's no rush. 1. Look at the word list on the left side. Press one word. A card opens for that word. There are 72 words, and you will do them one by one. Start with the first word. I expect you to press just one word and look at its card. 2. On the card, press Hear it. Listen carefully. Now say the word out loud yourself. Then press Again and say it one more time. Say it with your mouth, not just in your head. I expect to hear your voice two times for each word. 3. Now read the Meaning on the card. Press the little speaker next to it to hear the meaning read to you. Then say what the word means in your own words. Say it to a grown-up, or say it to yourself. I expect a short, simple answer, like "grandma is my mum's mum". 4. Next look at In a sentence. Read the sentence. Press Hear sentence to listen to it. Use the arrows to go through every sentence on the card. Then pick one sentence and read it out loud yourself, nice and clear. I expect one whole sentence said out loud by you. 5. Now look at the Spelling line. Look at the letters. Say each letter one by one, slowly. Then say the whole word again. I expect the letters said in order, then the word. 6. Now go to Write your own sentence. Type a sentence with the word in the box. The grey words give you a start, so you are not alone. Then press Check sentence. Read what the checker tells you. If it points something out, fix it and press Check sentence again. I expect a true sentence about your life, like "This is my grandma."

7. When you can say the word, know its meaning, and have written your sentence, press I know this word. Your word gets a LEARNED tag in the list. I expect you to press this only when all three parts are done — that is being honest, and honest work is good work. 8. Now press the next word in the list. Do the same steps again: Hear it, Again, Meaning, In a sentence, Spelling, Write your own sentence, I know this word. Keep going, one word at a time. I expect you to stop and rest when you feel tired, then come back. 9. Under the word list there is a deck of slides with the same words, one word on each slide. Press the Start button on the first slide, which says Say the words. On each slide, press Hear it and Again and say the word, press Meaning to hear what it means, read the sentences and press Hear sentence, look at the Spelling line, open Write your own sentence and type yours, press Check sentence, then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right for the next slide. The little dots under the slide show where you are. On the last slide, when every word is marked, press the finish button. The cards at the top and the slides at the bottom teach the same words — pick the one you like best. You will know the page is finished when every word in the list has a LEARNED tag next to it, and no word is left plain. Off you go — press your first word and press Hear it. Tell me which word you picked, and I will help you with it! 🌟

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Grammar page. This page has six little lessons. Each one teaches you a talking pattern about your family, like "This is my mum" and "I can help by sweeping." We do this so you can talk about your family in English with a big, confident voice. You need your voice, your ears, and maybe a family photo near you. What I expect from you is easy: say every word out loud, even quietly. Talking is the work here! Here is the whole page, step by step. 1. Start at the top with Lesson 1. Read the rule and look at the examples. Then press the speaker button to hear it read to you. If it goes too fast, press Replay and listen again. I expect you to listen right to the end, and not press anything else while it talks. 2. Now say the examples out loud yourself. Say them slowly, like the voice did. For Lesson 1 that is "This is my mother." Say the little word "is" clearly in the middle — it likes to hide! I expect your mouth to move, not just your eyes. 3. Under the lesson, press Show practice. Try the practice sentences on your own first. Put in real people from your family, like "This is my grandma." Then press Hear the practice and check if yours sounded the same. If it did not, say it again after the voice. That is not a mistake — that is practice. 4. Do steps 1, 2 and 3 again for Lesson 2, then Lesson 3, then 4, 5 and 6. Six lessons in all. Take a little rest between them if you get tired. Take your time — there's no rush. 5. Now go down to the slides at the bottom, called Say the patterns. Press Start. One pattern will come up on each slide, like "Do you like ___?"

6. On each slide, say the pattern out loud, then try the practice with your own words. Then press the speaker to hear it. Move to the next slide and do the same. Keep going all the way to the last slide. I expect one loud, brave try on every single slide. 7. When all six lessons and all the slides are done, press the button at the bottom that says I practised all the lessons. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed that button and it stops waiting for you. That is your work saved — well done! Ready? Go and do step 1 now, then come back and tell me one sentence you said out loud. 😊

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text: Hello! Today I am your speaking teacher. This page is our talking page. We will practise six family sentences out loud, like "This is my mum" and "I can help by sweeping". We do this so your mouth gets used to English words and your voice grows brave. You need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. Speak up so your recording can hear you! Here is our plan. There are six steps. Take your time — there's no rush. 1. Listen and say. There are 6 speaking practices on this page. For each one, press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear the model sentence. Listen two times. Then say it out loud yourself, big and clear. I expect a whole sentence, not one word — like "He is my brother", not just "brother". 2. Record your voice. Press the microphone button. Say the sentence slowly and clearly. Then press the microphone again to stop. I expect you to say the whole sentence in one go. If you giggle or stop, that is fine — just record again. 3. Listen to yourself. Play your recording back and listen. Ask yourself: can I hear every word? Did I sound happy and clear? I expect you to really listen, not skip this bit. Hearing your own voice is how you get better. 4. Submit and check. Press Submit for pronunciation check. This button turns on after you have listened back. Read what the checker tells you. If it says a word was not clear, record again and try that word slower. Do steps 1 to 4 for every one of the 6 practices. 5. The slides at the bottom. Under the practices there is a slide deck called Use your voice, with one practice on each slide. Press Start. Press Hear model and listen. Say it yourself out loud. Press Record, say your sentence, then press Submit. Press the arrow to go to the next practice. Keep going until the slides are done. 6. Finish. When all the practices and all the slides are done, press the Finish speaking practices button at the bottom of the page. You will know the page is finished when every practice has a recording you have listened to and submitted, the slides have no more arrows to press, and you have pressed Finish speaking practices. Then you can tell your grown-up one sentence you said today. Off you go — I am listening! 🎤

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Hello! Today we are doing Comprehension. That big word just means: I read the story, and I show that I understood it. We will think about "Breakfast at Grandma's House" — Amal, her baby brother Idris, the fruit, and the counting. By the end you will be able to answer questions about the story in your own words, and say your talk lines out loud. You need your listening ears, your voice, and a grown-up nearby if one can sit with you. There are five steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Look at the questions on the page. There are 12 of them. Read each one, or ask your grown-up to read it to you. Then close your eyes for a moment and picture the story. I expect you to think first, before you type. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 2. Type your answer in the box. Try to write a full sentence, not just one word. So instead of "Idris", write "His name is Idris." Some questions are talk lines, like "This is my ___." For those, fill in the gap with someone from your own family. I expect one honest, whole sentence in every box. Step 3. Press Check guidance. It will show you a good answer. Now compare: is your answer close to it? It does not have to match word for word — your own words are welcome! If your box is empty, the page will ask you to write something first, so always type before you press. Do this for every single question, all 12. Step 4. Now scroll down to the slides at the bottom. They say "Think about the story", with one question on each slide. Press Start. Say your answer out loud in a big, brave voice — this part is for talking, not typing. Then press Check guidance to see a good answer, and press the arrow to go to the next question. On the very last slide, press Finish comprehension. I expect your speaking voice, even if it is quiet. Step 5. Last of all, go back to the bottom of the page and press Finish comprehension. Only press it when every question has an answer and every slide is done. That button is yours to press, not mine. You will know the page is finished when all 12 boxes have your sentences in them, every slide has been spoken, and you have pressed Finish comprehension. Then you are done! Shall we start with question one? Tell me your answer and I will listen. 😊

writing.label: Writing
writing.text: Hello! Today I am your writing teacher. On this page you will write little sentences about your family. Writing helps you show your ideas on paper, not just say them. By the end, you will have written six small pieces of writing all by yourself. You need a quiet spot, your voice for saying words out loud, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. Let's go! Step one. Look at the list of writing tasks. There are six. Start with the first one and press it to open it. Read the task, or press Hear the task to listen to it. Say the task back to me in your own words. That is how I know you understand it. Step two. Press View model text. This shows one good example, like "This is my mum." Read it slowly. Look at the big letter at the start and the little dot at the end. I expect you to copy the shape of that sentence, not the same words. Your words should be about YOUR family. Step three. Now write in the big box. Say your sentence out loud first, then write it. Try to write at least eight words. That is a lot for Grade 1, so a grown-up can help you count on your fingers. Use the Writer's checklist to check yourself. If you feel stuck, press Support. If it feels easy, press Challenge and do a bit more. Step four. Press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved, so nothing is lost. You can come back and make it better any time. Then go back to the list and do the next task. Do all six tasks, one after another, in order. Step five. Now scroll down to the slides at the bottom. There is one task on each slide, called Plan, write and improve. Press Start. Write your sentences in the box, at least eight words again. Press Submit this draft. Then press the arrow to go to the next task, and do the same thing. You will know the page is finished when every writing task has been submitted, and every slide at the bottom has been submitted too. Then read one of your sentences out loud to a grown-up, or to yourself. Ready to start with task one? Tell me which task you can see first.

activities.label: Activities
activities.text: Hello! Today we are doing the Activities page for Family Time. These activities are the fun part — you point, say, draw, colour, act and count. We do them so the family words feel easy in your mouth: mum, dad, sister, brother, grandma, grandpa. By the end you will be able to name your family, count to ten, and say one way you help at home. You will need crayons, paper, and your talking voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. Here is the whole page, step by step. 1. There are 6 activities on this page. Read the words for each one, and press Hear the instructions to listen. Listen all the way to the end before you start. I expect you to know what to do before you begin — if you are not sure, press Hear the instructions again. 2. Now do the activity. In this unit you will point and name your family, draw yourself with your birthday number, colour the fruit, act out ways you help, count five plates, and make a thank-you card. Some activities have a box — type or write your answer there. I expect a real try, out loud where it says to speak. Say the whole sentence, like "This is my grandma", not just one word. 3. When you have finished one activity, press Mark complete under it. Only press it after you really did the activity. That button tells me you are done, so it must be true. 4. At the bottom of the page there is a slide deck called Learn by doing. It has one activity on each slide. Press Start, do the activity on that slide, then press Mark complete. Press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going slide by slide. On the very last slide, press Finish activities. 5. Last of all, press Finish activities at the bottom of the page. Do this only when all six activities say complete. Take your time — there is no rush. You will know the page is finished when every activity shows Mark complete done, the slides are all finished, and you have pressed Finish activities. Then you can tell a grown-up one thing you learned today. I am proud of you already — let's begin with activity one!

games.label: Games
games.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Games page of Family Time. 🎮

This page is where we play with our new words. We will play with family words like mum, dad, sister, brother, grandma and grandpa. We will also play with fruit words and with numbers one to ten. Games help the words stick in your head, and they make learning fun. Here is what I expect from you: say each word out loud as you play, take your time, and try again if you get it wrong. Mistakes are how we learn. You will need your voice, your eyes, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. There are three steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Press a game to open it. Look at the games on your screen and press the first one. Play it! You earn stars and XP for the answers you know. If a game feels hard, press the hint button and read the clue. You can also try again as many times as you like. I expect you to say the word out loud each time you tap it, like "grandma" or "banana". Step 2. Play every game at least once. Do not stop after one game. Go back and press the next game, then the next, until you have played them all. If you want more stars, press a game again and play it a second time. Your stars go up when you get more right. I expect you to finish every game on the page, even the tricky ones. Step 3. When you have played them all, press the button that says I have played them all. That button tells the page you are done. If you get every game perfect, the page will finish all by itself and you will not need to press it. I expect you to press it only after you really have played each game. How will you know the page is finished? You will see your stars and XP, and the page will move you on. That means you did it! Off you go with Step 1 — press your first game now. Come and tell me which game you played and what your favourite word was. 🌟

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text: Hello! Today is your Family Time checkpoint. That is a little quiz to show what you know about family words, food words, numbers and sounds. We do it so you can see how much you have learned. You do not need a pencil — just your eyes, your thinking, and your finger to tap. I will not tell you any answers, because these ones must come from you. And I know you can do it! Step 1. There are 10 questions on this page. Read one question at a time. Read the question twice before you answer. Then look at each choice and say it quietly to yourself. Ask: does this one match the question? Some questions ask about people in a family. Some ask which sentence sounds right. Some ask about the first sound in a word — say the word out loud and listen to the very first sound. Tap the one answer you think is best. I expect one answer for every question, and I expect you to think before you tap. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 2. When you have answered all ten, you will see your score. That tells you how many you got right. You pass when more than half are right. That means six or more out of ten. Look at your score and say it out loud, like "I got eight out of ten." I expect you to be proud of every question you tried, even the tricky ones. Step 3. If your score is not high enough, that is okay. Mistakes are how we learn. Press Try again and do the quiz one more time. This time, go slowly and read each question twice. Think about the family words we learned: mother, father, sister, brother, grandma, grandpa. I expect you to try your best again, not to hurry. Step 4. When your score is good, press Continue. That takes you to My progress, where you can see how well you are doing in this unit. You will know the page is finished when you have answered all ten questions, seen your score, and pressed Continue to go to My progress. Come back to me any time you want to practise before you start. Good luck — you've got this! 🌟

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text:
Hello! Today we are doing our Books page. This is our story time for Unit 2, Family Time. You will read a story about a family — people like mum, dad, grandma and grandpa. Reading stories helps you hear new words and see them too. All you need is your eyes, your ears, and your voice for saying words out loud. Let's go! Here is what I expect from you. Look at every picture. Say the words out loud, even quietly. If a word is new, that is fine — that is why we read. There are 3 steps. Step 1: Choose a book from the shelf. Look at the shelf on your screen. Tap the book you like best. A good choice is a book about family, like Breakfast at Grandma's House. I expect you to pick one book and open it. Just one — you can read more later. Step 2: Read it page by page. Press the arrow to go to the next page. If your book plays as a video, just watch and listen carefully. Tap the pictures to hear their sounds — this helps your ears learn the words. I expect you to read or listen to every page, not skip. Say the family words out loud when you see them: mum, dad, grandma, grandpa, sister, brother, baby. Step 3: Go right to the end, then press Finish book. When you reach the last page, look for the button that says Finish book and press it. That tells the page you are done. I expect you to reach the real ending first — no jumping to the last page early! How will you know the page is finished? When you press Finish book on the last page, this page is complete. One book is enough. If you enjoyed it, choose another book and read again — reading more is always a happy extra. 📚

Come back and tell me who was in your story!

overview.label: Overview
overview.text:
Hello! Today we start Unit 3: Fun and Games. 🎈

This first page is called Overview. Overview means "a first look". It shows you what you will learn: play words like bounce, roll, throw and catch, the parts of your body, and words like on, under and next to. We do this page first so you know what is coming. You only need your eyes, your ears, and your voice. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 1. Look at the top of the page and read the unit preview. That is the little bit of writing about this unit. If you see a Listen button, press it. Then follow the words with your finger while the voice reads. I expect you to listen right to the end, and then say out loud one thing you will learn. You can say it to your grown-up, or to me! Step 2. Now find the part called How to learn. There are four steps there. Read them, or ask your grown-up to read them to you. These four steps tell you how to work on every page of this unit. I expect you to look at all four, and to know which one comes first. Step 3. When you have looked at both parts, press the button I have previewed this unit. Then press Open vocabulary. That button takes you to the next page, where we learn our new words together. I expect you to press them in that order — first I have previewed this unit, then Open vocabulary. You will know this page is finished when you have pressed I have previewed this unit and the vocabulary page opens for you. Ready? Start with Step 1, and tell me one thing you will learn in this unit. 😊

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text:
Hello! Today we are learning the words for Unit 3, Fun and Games. These are words like bounce, catch, nose and under. Learning words is how we learn to talk, read and write in English. By the end of this page, you will be able to say each word, tell what it means, and use it in your own sentence. You will need your voice, so say the words out loud. Ask a grown-up to sit with you if one is nearby. Take your time — there is no rush. Here are the steps. Do them one at a time. 1. Look at the word list on the left side of your screen. There are 64 words. Press one word to open its card. Start with the first word. I expect you to do one word at a time, not jump around. 2. On the card, press Hear it. Listen carefully. Now say the word out loud yourself. Then press Again and say it one more time. Say it with your mouth, not just in your head — that is how your tongue learns it. 3. Now look at Meaning on the card. Read it, then press the little speaker next to it to hear it. Now tell me the meaning in your own words. It does not have to be perfect. Try like this: "Bounce means the ball goes down and comes back up."

4. Next look at In a sentence. Read the sentence, then press Hear sentence to listen to it. Use the arrows to see every sentence for that word. Then pick one sentence and read it out loud in a big, clear voice. 5. Now look at the Spelling line on the card. Say each letter one by one, slowly. Then say the whole word again. This helps your eyes and your ears work together. 6. Now the best part: Write your own sentence. Type a sentence with the word in the box. The grey words give you a start. Then press Check sentence. Read what the checker tells you, and fix anything it says. I expect a sentence about your own life, like "I catch the ball with my hands."

7. When you can say the word, tell its meaning, and you have written your sentence, press I know this word. The word gets a LEARNED tag in the list. Well done — that is one word finished! 8. Now press the next word in the list. Do all the same steps again: Hear it, Again, Meaning, In a sentence, Spelling, Write your own sentence, I know this word. Do a few words each day. Stop while it is still fun. 9. Under the word list there are slides with the same words, one word per slide. If you like slides better, press Start on the first slide, the one that says Say the words. On each slide press Hear it and Again, press Meaning, read the sentences and press Hear sentence, look at the Spelling line, open Write your own sentence and press Check sentence, then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right for the next slide. The dots under the slide show where you are. On the last slide, press the finish button. Cards or slides — both teach the same words, so choose the one you like. You will know the page is finished when every word in the list has a LEARNED tag next to it. Then all 64 words are yours! Now go and press your first word. Come back and tell me which word you chose, and I will help you with it. 😊

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 3, Fun and Games. This page is your video lesson. You will meet the words for playing, like bounce, roll, throw and catch. You will also hear body words, like hand, foot and nose. By the end, you will be able to say some of these words out loud with me. You need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a little space to move. Here are your three steps. Step 1. Press play on the video and watch it right to the end. Sit somewhere quiet so you can hear well. Look at the words at the bottom of the screen, called captions, and follow them with your eyes. I expect you to watch the whole video, not stop halfway. Watching all of it is how the words stick in your head. Step 2. Say the words out loud with the teacher in the video. When the teacher says "bounce", you say "bounce" too. Say it in a big, brave voice, not a whisper. You can do the action with your body as well — bounce, jump, clap, touch your nose. I expect you to speak, not just listen. Speaking is how your mouth learns English. Step 3. When the video is finished, press the button under it to go on to Vocabulary. Only press it after the video ends, so you do not miss anything. If you want, watch once more first — that is very good learning. I expect you to press the button yourself, so the page knows you are done. You will know this page is finished when the video has ended, you have said the words out loud, and you have pressed the button to Vocabulary. Then your next page will open. Ready? Press play now, and come back and tell me one word you heard. 🙂

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Hello! Today we are doing Comprehension. That means we think about the story we read and answer questions about it. Our story is "Amal and the Big Ball" — Amal, Samira and Leo, and the ball that got stuck in the tree. This helps you remember the story and say your ideas in full sentences. You will need your eyes to read, your voice to say, and your fingers to type. There are five steps. Here they all are. 1. There are 12 questions on this page. Read one question at a time. Think back to the story. Ask yourself: what really happened here? Take your time — there's no rush. I expect you to think first, before you type. 2. Now type your answer in the box. Write a full sentence, not just one word. So not "red" but "Amal's ball was red." Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop. A grown-up can help you type if you need. 3. Next, press Check guidance. This shows you a good answer. Look at it, then look at yours. Are they close? That is great! If they are different, that is fine too — mistakes are how we learn. If your box is empty, the page will ask you to write first, so always write your own answer before you press it. Do this for every one of the 12 questions. 4. Under the questions there are slides called "Think about the story". There is one question on each slide. Press Start. Read the question, then say your answer out loud with your big clear voice. Then press Check guidance to see a good answer. Then press the arrow to go to the next question. Keep going, slide by slide. On the very last slide, press Finish comprehension. 5. When you have answered them all, go to the bottom of the page and press Finish comprehension. That tells the page you are done. Only press it when every box has your writing in it. You will know the page is finished when all 12 boxes have your sentences, you have seen the guidance for each one, you have said every slide out loud, and you have pressed Finish comprehension. Then you are done! Now start with question one, and tell me your answer — I would love to hear it. 😊

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text: Hello! Today we are going to read together on the reading shelf. There are three texts here: a story about Amal and her big red ball, some talk lines to say out loud, and a fun rhyme. We read them so you can hear our new words — bounce, roll, throw, catch — and get ready for the questions later. You will need your eyes, your finger, and your voice. Let's start! 1. Read the text on the screen slowly. Say the words out loud if you can. Use your finger to touch each word as you read it. It is fine to go slowly — there is no rush. I expect you to try every word, even the tricky ones. 2. Now press Prepare audio. Wait a moment, then press the play button. Listen carefully and move your finger along the words. Try to whisper the words with the voice. I expect your finger and your ears to work together. 3. If a text is a listening text, listen first, then read it along with the voice. The story of this unit is Amal and the Big Ball. Read that one very carefully, because the Comprehension questions come from it. Ask yourself: who plays, and what happens to the ball? 4. Press Next text to go to the next one. Press Previous text if you want to go back. Read all three texts, not just one. I expect you to read every text on the shelf. 5. Look at the bottom of the page. There is a deck of slides with the same text, one page at a time. Press Start on the first slide, called Read the story. On each page, read it, or press the speaker to listen. Then press the arrow to turn the page. On the last page, press I have read this text. 6. When you have read all the texts, press Finished reading. That tells the page you are done. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I have read this text on the last slide and pressed Finished reading at the end. Then come and tell me one thing you liked in the story. Take your time — there's no rush.

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Grammar page. Grammar means the way we put words together to make a good sentence. On this page you will learn six sentence patterns from our unit Fun and Games, like "I can jump" and "Touch your nose". We do this so you can talk and play in English with a friend. You need your voice, your body for the actions, and your ears for listening. There are 5 steps. Let's start with something small. 1. Look at the first lesson box. Read the rule and the examples with me. Then press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear it read out loud. Listen carefully, all the way to the end. I expect you to listen once with a quiet mouth, and then you will be ready to speak. 2. Now say the examples out loud. Say them the way you heard them, nice and clear. Do the action too! Say "I can jump" and jump. Say "Touch your nose" and touch your nose. I expect a whole sentence, not one word — not just "jump", but "I can jump". 3. Under the lesson, press Show practice. Try each practice sentence out loud by yourself first. Then press Hear the practice to check how it sounds. If your words match, well done! If not, say it again with the audio. Do this for every one of the six lessons, one at a time. Take your time — there's no rush. 4. Go down to the slides at the bottom. This part is called Say the patterns. Press Start. On each slide there is one pattern. Say the pattern out loud, then try the practice, then press the speaker to hear it. Then go to the next slide. I expect you to keep going to the very last slide, saying every pattern with your own words. 5. When all six lessons and all the slides are done, press the I practised all the lessons button at the bottom of the page. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed that button and it shows your work is done. Then tell me one pattern you liked best, and we can play a little game with it. Great work today!

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text:
Hello! Today I am your speaking teacher. On this page you will practise talking in English out loud. We do this because English lives in your mouth, not just on paper. You will say six little sentences from our unit, like "I can jump," "Can you catch?" and "Touch your nose." By the end you will say them clearly and hear your own voice getting better. You need three things: your voice, your ears, and a quiet spot. A grown-up can sit with you to help you press the buttons. Ready? Here are all the steps. 1. Listen to the model. There are 6 speaking practices on this page. In the first one, press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear the sentence. Listen two times. The first time, just listen. The second time, watch how the words sound. Then say the sentence out loud yourself, in a big brave voice. I expect you to say the WHOLE sentence, like "I can run," not just "run."

2. Record your voice. Press the microphone button. Say the sentence clearly and not too fast. Then press the microphone again to stop. I expect one clear try, with your mouth open wide so the words come out strong. 3. Listen to yourself. Press play and listen to your own recording. Ask yourself: did I say every word? Was I loud enough? This is the part where you become your own teacher. I expect you to really listen, not skip it. 4. Submit and check. After you listen back, the Submit for pronunciation check button turns on. Press it. Then read what the checker says about your words. If you want to say it better, press the microphone and record again. Do steps 1 to 4 for every one of the 6 practices. Take your time — there's no rush. 5. Now the slides at the bottom. Under the practices there is a deck called Use your voice. It gives you one practice on each slide. Press Start. Press Hear model and listen. Say it yourself out loud. Press Record, say the sentence, then press Submit. Then press the arrow to go to the next practice. Keep going until the slides are done. 6. Finish. When you have done them all, press the Finish speaking practices button at the bottom of the page. You will know the page is finished when every practice has your recording, and you have pressed Finish speaking practices. Then you can tell your grown-up your favourite sentence. Off you go — start with practice one, and tell me when you have said it out loud. 🌟

writing.label: Writing
writing.text: Hello! Today I am your writing teacher for Unit 3, Fun and Games. On this page you write about play. You will use words like bounce, jump, catch, hand and foot. Writing helps you keep your ideas on paper so you can read them again. You need a pencil, paper if you like to draw, and your voice. Yes — your voice! We always say the sentence out loud first, then write it. What I expect from you: say it out loud first, then write it. Start with a big letter. End with a full stop. Try your best letters. A grown-up may sit with you and help. There are 5 steps. Here they all are. 1. Look at the list of 6 writing tasks. Pick one to start with — Writing 1 is a good first one. Read the task. If you see a speaker, press Hear the task and listen carefully. I expect you to know what the task asks before you write anything. 2. Press View model text. This shows you a good example, like "I can throw." Read it, and read it again. I expect you to notice the big letter at the start and the full stop at the end. Do not copy it word for word — it is there to show you the shape of a good sentence. 3. Now write your own in the big box. Say your sentence out loud first. Then write it, using the sentence starter, like "I can ___" or "This is my ___" or "I am ___ing." Try to make at least eight words in the box — you can write two little sentences to get there, like "I can jump. I can catch the big ball." Use the Writer's checklist to check your work. If you feel stuck, press Support. If it feels easy, press Challenge and do a bit more. 4. Press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved, so it will not get lost. You can come back later and make it better. Then go back to the list and do the next task, until you have done all six. I expect you to try every one, even the hard ones. 5. Now look at the slides at the bottom of the page — the deck called Plan, write and improve. There is one task on each slide. Press Start. Write your sentences in the box, at least eight words. Press Submit this draft. Then press the arrow to move to the next task, and do the same again. You will know the page is finished when every writing task has been submitted, and you have pressed the arrow all the way to the last slide and submitted that one too. Then read your favourite sentence out loud to a grown-up. Ready? Do step 1 now, and tell me which task you picked. 🙂

activities.label: Activities
activities.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Activities page. This page is all about Fun and Games. You will move your body, name body parts, and say where a ball is. Playing is how we learn these words best! You need a little space to move, a pencil or crayon, and your voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is near. Let's start. 1. There are 6 activities on this page. Read the words for each one. If reading is tricky, press Hear the instructions and listen carefully. I expect you to listen right to the end before you begin. Good listening makes the game easy. 2. Now do the activity. Some ask you to point, some ask you to move, and some ask you to write in the box. Say the word out loud while you do the action, like "bounce!" or "nose!" If there is a box, write one or two words in your neatest letters. I expect you to try, even if the word is a bit hard. Mistakes are how we learn. 3. When you have finished one activity, press Mark complete under it. Only press it after you really did it. That button tells me you are done. Then move to the next activity, until all 6 are marked complete. 4. Now look at the bottom of the page. There is a slide deck called Learn by doing. It has one activity on each slide. Press Start. Do that activity, then press Mark complete. Press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going, slide by slide. On the last slide, press Finish activities. I expect you to do every slide, not skip any. 5. Last of all, press Finish activities at the bottom of the page. Press it only when all 6 activities and all the slides are done. That is your big finish! You will know the page is finished when every activity has Mark complete pressed, and you have pressed Finish activities. Then you can tell me one thing you did today, like "I can bounce" or "This is my nose."

Ready? Start with activity one, and tell me when you have done it. Take your time — there's no rush.

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text: Hello! Today we are going to read a book together on this page. Reading books helps our Unit 3 words come alive — words like bounce, roll, catch, and on, under, next to. By the end, you will have read one whole book and heard lots of English. You need your eyes, your ears, and your voice. Ready? Here are the three steps. 1. Choose a book from the shelf. Look at the shelf on your screen. Look at the covers and pick the one you like best. Tap that book to open it. I expect you to choose with your own eyes — any book you like is a good choice. 2. Read it page by page. Press the arrow to go to the next page. Read slowly. Take your time — there's no rush. Say the words out loud if you can. If your book plays as a video, just watch and listen. Tap the pictures too — they make sounds! I expect you to listen carefully and try to say some words with the book. 3. Go right to the end, then press Finish book. Keep pressing the arrow until you reach the last page. On the last page you will see a button that says Finish book. Press it. I expect you to reach the very end, not stop in the middle. One book finishes this page — but you may read more if you want! You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Finish book on the last page. That is your work saved — well done! When you are done, come and tell me one thing that happened in your book. I would love to hear it. 📚

games.label: Games
games.text: Hello! Today we are on the Games page. This is our play page for Fun and Games. You will play little games with our words — words like bounce, roll, catch, and words for your body, like hand, nose and foot. We play because playing helps the words stick in your head. You need your eyes, your ears, and your happy voice. There are three steps. Let's start! Step 1. Look at the games on the screen. Press one game to open it. Now play! Take your time — there's no rush. You get stars and XP for the ones you know. If a game feels hard, press the hint button, or try again. Using a hint is smart, not naughty. I expect you to say each word out loud as you play. Step 2. Play every game at least once. Go back and press the next game, then the next, until you have opened them all. If you want more stars, play a game again — the second try is often better! I expect one honest try on every game, even the tricky ones. Step 3. When you have played them all, press the button that says I have played them all. Only press it when every game has really had a turn. That tells the page you are done. You will know the page is finished when you press that button — or when you master every game, and the page finishes all by itself. Ready? Press your first game now, and tell me which one you chose! 🌟

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text: Hello! This page is our Fun and Games checkpoint. That is a little quiz at the end of our unit. It has 10 questions about action words like bounce and clap, body words like nose, and place words like on and under. We do it to see what you already know. You need your eyes, your ears, and your thinking brain. A grown-up can read the questions out loud with you. Here is what I expect from you. Try every question by yourself. Read it twice. Then pick the one answer you think is best. I will not tell you the answers — but I promise you can get this. 1. Look at question one. Read it, or ask your grown-up to read it to you. Then read all four choices. Think: what is the question really asking? If it asks for an action word, pick the word your body can do — like run or jump, not a thing like a shoe. If it asks about a body part, touch that part on you and see if it fits. If it asks where the ball is, think of the ball on top, under, or beside. If it asks about rhyme, say the two words out loud and listen to the end sound. Then click the answer you choose. Do this the same way for all 10 questions, one at a time. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. When you finish the last question, you will see your score. That tells you how many you got right out of 10. More than half right means you passed. Read your score with your grown-up and be proud of every question you tried. 3. If your score is not high enough, do not worry. Mistakes are how we learn. Press Try again and do the quiz once more. This time go slowly and read each question twice. When your score is good, press Continue. That takes you to My progress. You will know the page is finished when you have seen your score and pressed Continue to go to My progress. Ready? Start with question one, and tell me when you have finished the quiz. 😊

overview.label: Overview
overview.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this is our Overview page. Overview means a little look at the whole unit before we start. Our unit is called Making Things. By the end of this page, you will know what we will learn, and how we will work. You need your eyes, your ears, and your voice. Let's start! Here is what I expect from you: look at the words, listen carefully, and say things out loud. Nobody has to be perfect. Trying is the win. There are three steps on this page. Step 1. Read the unit preview on this page. It tells you what you will learn in this unit — shapes, colours, clothes and making things from paper. If you see a Listen button, press it, and follow the words with your finger as you hear them. Do it well by listening all the way to the end, and by saying one word out loud with the voice. I expect you to find one thing that sounds fun and say, "I want to make that!"

Step 2. Read the four steps under How to learn. These four steps are how you will work on every page of this unit. Read them slowly, one at a time, and point to each one. A grown-up can read them with you if someone is near. I expect you to be able to say, in your own words, what you do first. Step 3. Press the button that says I have previewed this unit. That tells the page you have had your little look. Then press Open vocabulary. Vocabulary means our new words, and that page is next. Press gently and wait for the new page to come. You will know this page is finished when you have listened to the preview, read the four steps, pressed I have previewed this unit, and the vocabulary page has opened. Great work today! When the new page opens, come back and tell me one word you see there.

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Vocabulary page of Unit 4, Making Things. This page holds 72 words: shapes, colours, clothes, making words, and story words. We learn them so you can say what you make, what colour it is, and what you are wearing. By the end you will hear each word, say it, know what it means, and write your own sentence with it. You need your voice, your ears, and your fingers for typing. Say every word out loud — not in your head. That is what I expect from you today. Here are all the steps. Take your time — there's no rush. 1. Look at the word list on the left side. Press one word. A card opens for that word. Start with the first word and work down. You will do all 72 words, one at a time. I expect you to do one word properly, then move on — not rush through many. 2. On the card, press Hear it. Listen carefully. Now say the word out loud yourself. Then press Again and say it one more time. I want to hear your voice, loud and clear, both times. 3. Now read the Meaning on the card. Press the little speaker next to it to hear the meaning read to you. Then say what the word means in your own words. It does not have to match the card. If you can say it your way, you really know it. 4. Next, look at In a sentence. Read a sentence. Press Hear sentence to listen to it. Use the arrows to go through every sentence on the card. Then pick one sentence and read it out loud yourself. Nice and slow, like a storyteller. 5. Now look at the Spelling line on the card. Say each letter, one by one, out loud. Then say the whole word again. Letters first, then the word — that helps your hand remember it later. 6. Now Write your own sentence. Type a sentence with the word in the box. The grey words give you a start. Press Check sentence. Read what the checker tells you, and fix anything it points out. Use a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end. 7. When you can say the word, know its meaning, and have written your sentence, press I know this word. The word gets a LEARNED tag in the list. Only press it when all three are true — that is your promise to yourself. 8. Now press the next word in the list. Do steps 2 to 7 again for that word. Same steps every time. A few words each day is better than all of them at once. 9. Under the word list there is a deck of slides. It has the same words, one word on each slide. On the first slide, called Say the words, press Start. On each slide press Hear it and Again, press Meaning, read the sentences and press Hear sentence, look at the Spelling line, open Write your own sentence, type your sentence and press Check sentence, then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right for the next slide. The dots under the slide show where you are. On the last slide, when every word is marked, press the finish button. The card at the top and the slides at the bottom teach the same words — pick the one you like best. You will know the page is finished when every single word in the list has a LEARNED tag next to it.
