If you used the slides, you will also have pressed the finish button on the last slide. Ready to press your first word? Tell me which word you opened, and we will do it together. 🙂

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 4, Making Things. This page is your video lesson. You will watch, listen, and say words out loud with the teacher in the video. By the end you will know some shape words, colour words and clothes words. You need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a grown-up nearby if one can sit with you. Let's start! 1. Press the play button on the video. Then watch it all the way to the end. Sit still and listen carefully. Words will show at the bottom of the screen — these are called captions. Try to look at them while you listen. I expect you to watch the whole video, not stop in the middle. 2. Say the words out loud with the teacher. When the teacher says "circle", you say "circle" too. When she says "I am cutting paper", you say it too. Say it in a big, clear voice. Do not just whisper. If a word is hard, that is fine — say it again after her. I expect to hear your voice, not just your ears working! 3. When the video is finished, press the button under the video to go on to Vocabulary. That takes you to the next part of our unit, where we learn the words more closely. Only press it after the video has really ended. You will know this page is finished when the video has played to the end, you have said the words out loud with the teacher, and you have pressed the button to go to Vocabulary. Off you go — press play. Tell me when you have finished watching, and tell me one word you heard. 😊

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Hello! Today we are doing Comprehension. That word means "showing what you understood." You will think about our story, Amal Makes a Mat, and about our talk lines. Talking about a story helps you remember it and helps you make your own sentences. You need your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up nearby if one is there. Here is what I expect from you. Try every question by yourself first. Answer in a full sentence, like "Amal is making a mat." Do not worry about perfect spelling. Trying is the most important part. There are 5 steps. Here they are. 1. Read the first question. There are 12 questions on this page. Read it slowly, or ask your grown-up to read it with you. Then think about the story for a moment. Ask yourself: what happened in that part? Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Type your answer in the box. Write a full sentence, not just one word. So instead of "mat", write "Amal is making a mat." Use words from the story if you can. I expect one good sentence in the box before you move on. 3. Press Check guidance. This shows you a good answer. Read it and compare it with yours. If your answer means the same thing, say "yes!" — you got it. If it is different, that is fine; mistakes are how we learn. Remember: the box must have your writing in it first, or the page will ask you to write something. Do steps 1, 2 and 3 again for all 12 questions. 4. Now go to the slides at the bottom. This part is called Think about the story. Press Start. One question shows on each slide. Say your answer out loud in a big, clear voice. Then press Check guidance to see a good answer, and press the arrow to go to the next question. On the very last slide, press Finish comprehension. 5. When every question has an answer, press Finish comprehension at the bottom of the page. That tells the page you are done. You will know the page is finished when all 12 boxes have your sentences, you have said every slide out loud, and you have pressed Finish comprehension. Then you can smile — you did it! Ready? Start with question one, and tell me your answer. I am right here. 😊

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Grammar page. Let's look at that together. On this page you learn six little sentence patterns. A pattern is a sentence shape you can fill in, like "This is a ___." We do this so you can talk about the things you make, the colours you use, and the clothes you wear. By the end you will say six sentences all by yourself. What you need: your ears, your voice, and a grown-up nearby if one can sit with you. What I expect: you say every sentence OUT LOUD, not just in your head. Loud and proud, even if it is not perfect. Mistakes are how we learn. There are five steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Read the six lessons. Start at the first lesson at the top. Read the rule and the examples. Then press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear it read to you. Listen carefully. The six patterns are: This is a ___. It is a ___ ___. I am cutting ___. I am making ___. I am wearing ___. I can be a ___. I expect you to listen to each lesson at least once before you move down the page. Step 2. Say the examples out loud. After you hear a lesson, say the same words back. Say it slowly, like this: "This is a box." "This is an apron." Try to make your voice sound like the voice you heard. A good try is a clear, slow sentence with every word in it. Do not drop the little word "am" — we say "I am cutting paper," not "I cutting paper."

Step 3. Do the practice in every lesson. Under each lesson, press Show practice. Try the practice sentences out loud. Then press Hear the practice to check how they sound. Did your sentence sound the same? If not, say it once more. Do this for all six lessons, one after the other. I expect three sentences from you in each lesson, not just one. Step 4. Do the slides at the bottom. Under the lessons there is a slide deck called Say the patterns. Press Start. One pattern comes up on each slide. Say the pattern out loud, try the practice, then press the speaker to hear it. Then go to the next slide. Keep going to the very last slide. Here is my hint for these: put your own real things in the gap. Look at your clothes and say, "I am wearing a shirt." Look at your work and say, "I am making a card."

Step 5. Finish the page. When all six lessons and all the slides are done, press the I practised all the lessons button at the bottom. Only press it after you have really said everything out loud, because that button tells your teacher what you did. How will you know the page is finished? When every lesson has been heard and practised, when the slides have reached the last one, and when you have pressed I practised all the lessons. Off you go with Step 1. Tell me when you have listened to the first lesson, and tell me one sentence you said out loud. 😊

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text:
Hello! Today I am your reading teacher. 📖

This page is our reading shelf. There are 3 texts on it. One is our story, Amal Makes a Mat. One is our talk lines. One is our rhyme. We read them to meet new words like circle, weave and patient, and to enjoy a good story. What I expect from you: read slowly, say the words out loud if you can, and point at each word with your finger. Slow and careful is best — just like Amal and her mat! You need your eyes, your voice, your finger, and a quiet spot. Ready? Here are our 6 steps. 1. Read the text on the screen. Start at the top. Read slowly, one word at a time. Read out loud if you can — your ears help your reading! If a word is tricky, sound it out, then say it again. I expect you to reach the very end of the text, not just the first line. 2. Now let the text read to you. Press Prepare audio. Wait a moment. Then press the play button. Listen carefully and move your finger under the words as they are said. I expect your finger and the voice to stay together. If you fall behind, press play again and try one more time. 3. Some texts are for listening first. If a text says listening, listen all the way through, then read along with the voice the second time. One text is our unit story, Amal Makes a Mat. That is the one the Comprehension questions ask about, so read that one extra carefully. I expect you to know who made the mat and how it felt at the end. 4. Now move along the shelf. Press Next text to go to the next one. Press Previous text to go back. Read every text — all 3. Do not skip one! I expect you to say, "I read them all."

5. Look at the bottom of the page. There is a deck of slides with the same text, one page at a time. On the first slide, press Start. On each page, read the words, or press the speaker to hear them. Then press the arrow to turn the page. Keep going to the last page. On the last page, press I have read this text. 6. When all 3 texts are read, press Finished reading. That tells the page you are done. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I have read this text on the slides, and then Finished reading. Take your time — there's no rush. Come and tell me when step 1 is done, and tell me one word you liked in the story. 🌟

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text:
Hello! Today I am your speaking teacher, and this page is all about your voice. 🎤

We are doing speaking practice because talking out loud is how English gets easy. You will hear the words, say them back, and hear yourself. By the end you will be able to say six making sentences all by yourself, like "This is a circle" and "I am wearing a hat."

You need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby to help press the buttons. Take your time — there's no rush. Here is what I expect from you: say every sentence out LOUD, not in your head. Say it slowly and clearly, like you are telling someone across the room. Trying is the win, not being perfect. There are 6 steps on this page. Here they all are. 1. Listen and say. There are 6 speaking practices on this page. In each one, press the speaker button or Replay to hear the model sentence. Listen two times. Then say the same sentence out loud yourself. I expect a big clear voice, and every word said — do not leave out the little word "am" in "I am cutting."

2. Record yourself. Press the microphone button. Say your sentence. Then press the microphone again to stop. Wait one small second before you start talking, so the beginning of your word is not cut off. 3. Listen to you. Play your recording back and listen to yourself. Ask yourself one thing: can I hear every word clearly? This is my favourite part — you get to be the teacher of your own voice! 4. Submit and check. Press Submit for pronunciation check. This button turns on after you have listened back, so do step 3 first. Read what the checker tells you, and if you want to do better, just record again. Do steps 1, 2, 3 and 4 for every one of the 6 practices. 5. The slides at the bottom. Under the practices there is a slide deck called Use your voice, with one practice on each slide. Press Start. Press Hear model, then say it yourself out loud. Press Record, then press Submit. Then press the arrow to go to the next practice. Keep going until you have done every slide. 6. Finish. When all the practices and all the slides are done, press the Finish speaking practices button at the bottom of the page. You will know the page is finished when every practice has a recording, you have pressed Submit on each one, the slides are all done, and you have pressed Finish speaking practices. Now go and do step 1 — listen twice, then say it out loud. Come back and tell me which sentence felt easiest to say! 😊

writing.label: Writing
writing.text:
Hello, my Grade 1 writer! Today I am your teacher for the Writing page in Unit 4, Making Things. On this page you write small words and sentences about things you make. You will use our unit words: shapes like circle and square, colours like red and gold, and clothes like hat and shoes. Why do we do it? Because saying a word is good, and writing it makes it stick in your head. By the end you will be able to write short sentences like "This is a hat." and "I am making a card."

What I expect from you: say your sentence out loud first, then write it. Start with a capital letter. Leave a small space between words. Put a full stop at the end. Neat is nice, but brave is better — a try is always a win. Get your pencil and paper ready too, because some tasks ask you to draw. Here are all the steps. Take them one at a time. Step 1. Look at the list of writing tasks. There are 6 of them. Press the first one to open it. Read the task, and if you see a speaker button, press Hear the task and listen carefully. I expect you to know two things before you write: what to write, and what to draw. Step 2. Press View model text. This shows you an example of good writing, like "This is a hat." Look at how it begins with a big capital letter and ends with a full stop. Do not copy it word for word. Copy the shape of it, and put your own idea inside. Step 3. Now write your own in the big box. Write at least eight words — that is about two short sentences. Use the sentence starter given, like "This is a" or "I am making". Then read the Writer's checklist and check your work: capital letter, spaces, full stop. If you feel stuck, press Support for extra help. If it feels easy, press Challenge and write one more sentence. Step 4. Press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved, so nothing is lost. You can come back later and make it even better. Then go back to the list and do the next task, one after another, until all 6 are done. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 5. Now scroll down to the slides at the bottom of the page. This deck is called Plan, write and improve, and it has one task on each slide. Press Start. Write your sentences in the box — again, at least eight words. Press Submit this draft. Then press the arrow to go to the next task, and do the same thing again. You will know the page is finished when all 6 writing tasks have a saved draft, and every slide in the deck has been submitted too. Then read your favourite sentence out loud to a grown-up if one is nearby, or to yourself. Great work today! Come back any time you want to practise. 😊

activities.label: Activities
activities.text: Hello! Today we are on the Activities page for our unit, Making Things. Here is what this page is. There are six little activities. You will name shapes, name colours, talk about clothes, and make things with paper. We do this so you can say the words out loud and use your hands, because that is how new words stick. What I expect from you: try every activity, say the words out loud, and do your best work. Neat is nice, but trying is what matters most. You will need crayons, paper, and safe scissors with a grown-up nearby. Here are all the steps. 1. First, read the instructions for each activity. There is a button called Hear the instructions. Press it and listen carefully. You can press it again if you want to hear it twice. I expect you to listen right to the end before you start. 2. Now do the activity. Some activities have a box for writing. Say your answer out loud first, then write it in the box. Short is fine, even one or two words. I expect a real answer from you, not an empty box. 3. When you have finished one activity, press Mark complete under it. Only press it when you have really done the work. Do this for each of the six activities, one at a time. 4. Look under the activities. There is a slide deck called Learn by doing, with one activity on each slide. Press Start. Do that activity, then press Mark complete. Then press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going like that, slide by slide. On the very last slide, press Finish activities. 5. Last of all, go to the bottom of the page and press Finish activities. Press it only when every activity has its Mark complete. You will know the page is finished when all six activities say complete, all the slides are done, and you have pressed Finish activities at the bottom. Take your time — there's no rush. Tell me when you are on activity one, and I will help you with it.

games.label: Games
games.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Games page. This page is where we play with our Unit 4 words: shapes like circle and square, colours like red and gold, clothes like hat and dress, and our talking lines "I am cutting..." and "I am making...". Games help the words stick in your head, because playing is a very good way to remember. By the end, you will know these words faster and feel proud. You need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a grown-up nearby if you want one. Here is what I expect from you: try your best, say each word out loud as you play, and never worry about mistakes. Mistakes are how we learn. Step 1. Look at the games on your screen. Press one game to open it. Any game is fine — pick the one that looks fun. Then play it. You earn stars and XP for the answers you know. If a question is hard, press the hint button, or try again. Hints are there to help you, so please use them. I expect you to say the word out loud each time you tap it, like "circle" or "yellow". Step 2. Now play every game on the page, at least one time each. Go back and press the next game, then the next, until you have opened them all. Take your time — there is no rush. When a game is done, you can play it again to win more stars. I expect you to finish each game you start, even if it feels tricky. Playing twice is a great way to get better. Step 3. When you have played all the games, press the button that says I have played them all. Only press it when you really have played every one. If you master every single game, the page will finish all by itself, and you will not need to press it. You will know the page is finished when your games show their stars and the page tells you it is complete, after you press I have played them all. Now go and press your first game. When you finish it, come back and tell me which game you played and one word you learned. 🌟

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text: Hello! This page is our Making Things checkpoint. It is a little quiz with 10 questions about shapes, colours, clothes and making words. We do it to see what you can already do all by yourself. I will not give you answers — but I will show you how to think. You just need your eyes, your ears, and a grown-up nearby if you like. Here is what I expect from you today: try every question, even the tricky ones. Take your time. Guessing your best try is always better than nothing. Step 1. Read the first question, or ask your grown-up to read it to you. Then look at all the choices before you pick. Ask yourself, "What is this question really asking?" If it says "shape", look for a shape word like circle or square. If it says "colour", look for a colour word like green. When you are sure, click the answer you choose. I expect you to look at every choice first, not just the first one. Step 2. Keep going, one question at a time. Some questions ask about sides and corners. Draw the shape in the air with your finger and count the sides out loud. Three sides is one shape, four the same sides is another, and round with no corners is another. Some questions ask about tools — think about what scissors do and what glue does. Some ask about a sentence, like cutting, making or wearing. Remember: wearing means it is on your body already. Step 3. When you finish all 10 questions, your score will show on the screen. You pass with more than half right. That means 6 or more out of 10. Look at your score and read it out loud to your grown-up. Step 4. If your score is not high enough, press Try again. Do the quiz once more, slowly. This is not a sad thing at all — trying again is exactly what Amal did with her bumpy mat! Mistakes are how we learn. Step 5. When your score is good, press Continue. That takes you to My progress, and it means your work is saved. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Continue and you can see My progress on your screen. Good luck — you know more than you think! 🌟

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text: Hello! Today I am your reading teacher. This is our Books page for Unit 4, Making Things. Here you pick a book and read it all the way through. Reading helps you meet our unit words like circle, square, hat and making. By the end, you will have read one whole book by yourself. You just need your eyes, your voice and a comfy seat. Here is what I expect from you. Read slowly. Say the words out loud if you can. Look hard at the pictures. And do not rush — good readers take their time, just like Amal did with her mat. There are three steps. Here they all are. 1. Choose a book from the shelf. Look at the books on the screen. Read the titles, or look at the covers. Tap the one you want. Try to pick a book about making things, like Amal Makes a Mat. Good choosing means you picked a book you really want to read, not just the first one you saw. 2. Read your book page by page. Press the arrow to go to the next page. Press the other arrow to go back if you want to read a page again. Tap the pictures to hear their sounds. Say the words out loud, slowly, one at a time. If a word is hard, sound it out or ask your grown-up. I expect you to look at every page, not skip any. Try to spot our unit words: circle, square, triangle, red, blue, hat, making. Some books may play like a video. If yours does, just watch and listen carefully, and join in with any words you know. 3. Finish your book. Keep going until you reach the very last page. On the last page, press Finish book. That tells the page you are done. Only press it when you really have reached the end — that is what makers do, they finish their work. One book finishes this page. But if you loved it, you may read another one. More reading is always good! You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Finish book on the last page of your book. That is the moment your work is saved. Now off you go — choose your book. When you have finished it, come back and tell me one thing you liked. 📚

overview.label: Overview
overview.text:
Hello! Welcome to Unit 5: On the Farm. 🐄

This page is called Overview. Overview means "a first look". It is like standing at the gate of a farm and looking in before you go inside. We do this so you know what is coming. By the end of this page you will know what you will learn, and you will be ready to start. You need your eyes, your ears, and your voice. That is all! There are three steps. Here they are. Step 1. Read the unit preview on this page. The preview tells you what you will learn about the farm. Look for a Listen button. If you see it, press Listen and follow the words with your finger as you hear them. Do it well by going slowly and saying one or two words out loud with the voice. I expect you to find one thing that sounds fun to you, like the animal sounds or the story. Step 2. Read the four steps under How to learn. These four steps tell you how you will work on every page of this unit. Read them one at a time, not all in a rush. A grown-up can read them with you if one is nearby. I expect you to be able to tell me, in your own words, what you do first. Step 3. Press the button that says I have previewed this unit. That button tells the page, "Yes, I have looked!" Then press Open vocabulary. Vocabulary means our new words. That button takes you to the next page, where we meet the farm words. I expect you to press them in that order: first I have previewed this unit, then Open vocabulary. You will know this page is finished when you have pressed I have previewed this unit and the vocabulary page opens on your screen. Ready? Start with Step 1, and tell me when you have looked at the preview. Take your time — there's no rush.

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Vocabulary page of On the Farm. 🐮

This page teaches you the farm words: animals like cow and hen, sounds like moo and baa, and farm things like barn, tractor and seed. We do it so you can SAY these words out loud with a big, brave voice. By the end you will know 53 words and be able to use them in your own sentences. You need your voice, your eyes, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. Let's start with something small. Here is the whole page, step by step. 1. Find the word list on the left side of your screen. Press the first word. A card opens up with everything about that word. You will do one word at a time, all the way to 53. I expect you to start with the very first word, not jump around. 2. On the card, press Hear it. Listen carefully. Now say the word out loud yourself. Then press Again and say it one more time. Out loud, please — not quietly in your head! I expect to hear your voice two times for every word. 3. Now look at the word Meaning on the card. Read it, or ask your grown-up to read it with you. Press the little speaker next to it to hear it. Then say what the word means in your OWN words. For example, for cow you might say, "It is big and it gives us milk." That is a great answer. 4. Next is In a sentence. Read the sentence on the card. Press Hear sentence to listen to it. Then press the arrows to see every sentence for that word. Pick one sentence you like and read it out loud. Loud and clear, like a story reader! 5. Now look at the Spelling line on the card. Say each letter one by one, slowly. C... O... W. Then say the whole word again: cow! I expect the letters said one at a time, then the word all together. 6. Now it is your turn to write. Find the box that says Write your own sentence. The grey words give you a start, so you are not alone. Type a short sentence with your word in it. Then press Check sentence. Read what the checker tells you and fix anything it points out. A short sentence is perfect — you do not need a long one. 7. When you can say the word, know what it means, and have written your sentence, press I know this word. The word gets a LEARNED tag in the list. Only press it when all three are true. That tag is your proof! 8. Now press the next word in the list. Do steps 2 to 7 again for that word. Same steps, new word, every time. Take your time — there's no rush. You can stop and come back later. 9. Under the word list there is a deck of slides. It has the same words, one word on each slide. On the first slide it says Say the words — press Start to begin. On each slide press Hear it and Again, press Meaning, read the sentences and press Hear sentence, look at the Spelling line, open Write your own sentence and press Check sentence, then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right to move to the next slide. The little dots under the slide show you where you are. On the last slide, when every word is marked, press the finish button. The cards at the top and the slides at the bottom teach the same words — you can pick whichever one you like best. How will you know you are finished? Look at the word list. When EVERY word has a LEARNED tag next to it, the page is done. If you used the slides, you will also have pressed the finish button on the last slide. Go and press your first word now. When you have done step 2 for it, come back and tell me which word you chose. 🐔

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 5, On the Farm. This page is our video lesson. You will watch, listen, and say farm words out loud — words like cow, hen, barn and tractor. We do this so your ears hear the words first, and then your mouth can say them with a big, happy voice. You need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a comfy seat. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. There are three steps. Here they are. 1. Press play on the video and watch it all the way to the end. Sit still and keep your eyes on the screen. Read the captions — those are the words at the bottom of the video. If a bit goes too fast, you can play it again. I expect you to watch right to the end without stopping halfway. 2. Say the words out loud with the teacher in the video. When the teacher says "cow", you say "cow" too. When she says a whole sentence, like "This is a cow", say the whole sentence with her. Make the animal sounds big and happy — moo, cluck, quack, baa! I expect your voice, not a quiet mouth. Mistakes are how we learn, so just try. 3. When the video has finished, press the button under it to go on to Vocabulary. That takes you to the word page, where we learn our farm words one by one. I expect you to press it only after the video is truly done. You will know this page is finished when the video has ended, you have said the words out loud with the teacher, and you have pressed the button to go to Vocabulary. Ready? Press play now, and come back and tell me one animal you saw. 🐄

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text:
Hello! Today I am your reading teacher. 🌾

This page is our reading shelf. It has 3 texts about the farm. One is the story "Amal and the Little Hen", one is a talk-and-point page, and one is our song and poem. We read them so farm words like cow, barn, seed and egg become easy in your mouth. Here is what I expect from you. Read slowly. Say the words out loud if you can. Point with your finger as you go. It is okay to get stuck — just try again. You need your eyes, your voice, your finger, and a quiet spot. Ready? Here are all the steps. 1. Look at the text on the screen. Read it slowly, from the top to the bottom. Read it out loud if you can, even in a small voice. Do not rush — slow reading is good reading. 2. Now let the words be read to you. Press Prepare audio. Wait a moment. Then press the play button. Listen carefully and move your finger under each word as you hear it. Try to whisper along. 3. If a text is a listening text, listen first, then read it again with your eyes. One text is our unit story, "Amal and the Little Hen". The Comprehension questions come from that story, so read that one extra carefully. Ask yourself: who is in the story, and what did they do? 4. Press Next text to go to the text after this one. Press Previous text to go back if you want to hear one again. Read every single text — all 3. Do not skip one, even a short one. 5. Now look under the reading. There is a deck of slides with the same words, one page at a time. On the first slide, press Start (it says Read the story). On each page, read the words, or press the speaker to hear them. Then press the arrow to turn the page. Keep going to the very last page. On the last page, press I have read this text. 6. When you have read all 3 texts and finished the slides, press Finished reading. You will know the page is done when you have pressed I have read this text on the slides and then Finished reading. That button is yours to press — I cannot press it for you. 😊

Start with step 1 now. Take your time — there's no rush.

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Hello! Today we are doing Comprehension. That means we talk about the story we read — "Amal and the Little Hen" — and show that we understood it. It helps you remember the story and say your ideas in full sentences. You need your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up nearby if you want help reading. Let's go, step by step! 1. Look at the first question. There are 12 questions in all. Read the question, or ask your grown-up to read it to you. Then close your eyes for a moment and think about the farm story. I expect you to think first, before you type. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Now type your answer in the box. Say it out loud first, then write it. Please write a full sentence, not just one word. So not "cow" but "They saw the cow first." I expect one clear sentence that answers the question. 3. Now press Check guidance. This shows you a good answer. Read it and compare it with yours. If your box is empty, the page will ask you to write first — so always write before you press. Do this for every question, all 12. If your answer is different, that is okay. Mistakes are how we learn. Just look at what was different and say the good answer out loud once. 4. Under the questions there is a deck of slides called Think about the story. It has one question on each slide. Press Start. Read the question, then say your answer out loud in a big, brave voice. Then press Check guidance to see a good answer. Press the arrow to go to the next question. Keep going, one slide at a time. On the last slide, press Finish comprehension. I expect you to speak every answer out loud, not just think it — speaking is how your English gets strong. 5. Last of all, go to the bottom of the page and press Finish comprehension. Only press it when you have answered all 12 questions and finished the slides. You will know the page is finished when every question box has your sentence in it, you have pressed Check guidance for each one, the slides are done, and you have pressed Finish comprehension. Then you're all done! Now start with question one, and tell me when you have typed your first answer. I'll be right here. 🌟

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Grammar page in our farm unit. Grammar means the way we put words together to make a good sentence. On this page we learn six farm sentence patterns, like "This is a cow" and "The hen is pecking." We do this so you can talk about the farm out loud, in whole sentences, with a big brave voice. You need your voice, your ears, and a chair to sit in. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. What I expect from you: say every sentence OUT LOUD, not just in your head. Talk slowly and clearly. It is fine to make mistakes — mistakes are how we learn. Here are all the steps. 1. Look at the six lessons on the page. Start with lesson one. Read the rule and the examples, and press the speaker button or Replay to hear it read to you. Listen carefully the first time. If it was fast, press Replay again — you may press it as many times as you like. I expect you to know one thing after each lesson: what the pattern is, like "This is a ___."

2. Now say the examples out loud. Say each one slowly, like this: "This is a cow." Take a breath, then say the next one. Make your voice happy and clear, so someone across the room could hear you. I expect three clear sentences from you in each lesson, not whispers. 3. Under the lesson, press Show practice. Try the practice sentences all by yourself, out loud. Then press Hear the practice to check how they sound. Ask yourself: did my sentence sound the same? Do this for every lesson, one to six. Do not skip a lesson, even an easy one — practice is what makes it stick. 4. Here is a little helper for the six patterns. Lesson one is "This is a ___" for naming an animal. Lesson two is "The ___ says ___" for animal sounds, so say the animal first, then the sound. Lesson three is "The ___ is ___ing" for what is happening now — do not forget the little word "is". Lesson four is "It has ___" for animal parts, like "It has soft wool." Lesson five is "First ___, then ___" for putting two farm jobs in order. Lesson six is "I can see a ___" for naming what you spot. 5. Now go to the slides at the bottom of the page, called Say the patterns. There is one pattern on each slide. Press Start to begin. On each slide, say the pattern out loud, then try the practice, then press the speaker to hear it. Move on to the next slide and do the same thing again. I expect you to keep going all the way to the last slide. 6. When the slides are finished, press the button at the bottom that says I practised all the lessons. Only press it after you have really done every lesson and every slide. That button is how the page saves your good work — I cannot press it for you. You will know the page is finished when all six lessons have been read and said, all the slides are done to the very last one, and the I practised all the lessons button has been pressed. Ready? Start with lesson one, and press the speaker. Come back and tell me when you have said your first sentence out loud — I would love to hear which animal you chose! 🐄

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text: Hello! Today I am your speaking teacher, and this is our Speaking page for On the Farm. On this page you will say farm sentences out loud, record your voice, and listen to yourself. We do this because English lives in your mouth, not just on the page — talking is how it becomes yours. You will need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby to help with the buttons. Here is the whole plan, step by step. 1. Listen and say. There are 6 speaking practices on this page. For each one, press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear the model sentence. Listen two times. Then say it out loud yourself, nice and clear, like you are talking to a friend across the room. Your six sentences are: This is a cow. The cow says moo. The duck is swimming. It has soft wool. First we feed the hens, then we collect the eggs. I can see a goat. I expect you to open your mouth wide and say every word — not a whisper! 2. Record your voice. Press the microphone button. Say your sentence, then press the microphone again to stop. Take a breath first, then speak slowly. A good recording is one whole sentence, with no long quiet bit at the start. I expect one full sentence, not just one word. 3. Listen to yourself. Press play and listen to your own recording. Ask yourself: can I hear every word clearly? This is my favourite step, because you become your own teacher. I expect you to listen right to the end, even if it feels funny hearing your voice. 4. Submit and check. Press Submit for pronunciation check. This button turns on after you have listened back, so do step 3 first. Read what the checker says about your words. If you want to do better, press the microphone and record again — that is allowed and it is smart! Do steps 1 to 4 for every one of the 6 practices. 5. The slides at the bottom. Under the practices there is a slide deck called Use your voice, with one practice on each slide. Press Start. Then press Hear model and listen. Say it yourself out loud. Press Record, say your sentence, then press Submit. Press the arrow to go to the next practice. Keep going until you have done every slide. I expect you to say it out loud before you record, every time — practice first, then record. 6. Finish. When all 6 practices and all the slides are done, press the Finish speaking practices button at the bottom of the page. Only press it at the end, because that is how the page saves your good work. You will know the page is finished when every practice has a recording you have listened to and submitted, the slides are all done, and you have pressed Finish speaking practices. Take your time — there's no rush. Come back and tell me which sentence felt the hardest, and we will practise that one together. 🐄

writing.label: Writing
writing.text:
Hello! Today I am your writing teacher. Let's do the Writing page together. On this page you do six little writing jobs about the farm. You will draw, trace, copy, label, and write your own farm sentence. Writing helps your hand and your brain remember the farm words like cow, hen, barn and field. By the end you will have written your very own sentence and read it out loud. You need a pencil, some paper, crayons if you like, and your happy voice. Here is what I expect from you today: say the words out loud first, then write. Neat is nice, but brave is better. Short is fine — eight words is plenty. Step 1. Look at the list of writing tasks. There are 6. Press the first task to open it. If you see a speaker, press Hear the task and listen carefully. I expect you to listen right to the end, then tell yourself in your own words what the task wants. Task 1 asks you to draw a farm with two animals and one plant, and say "This is a ___."

Step 2. Press View model text. This shows you a good example, like "This is a cow." Read it, or ask your grown-up to read it with you. Do not copy it word for word. I expect you to use it as a helper, the way you use a picture on the wall. Step 3. Now write in the big box. Try to write at least eight words. Say your sentence out loud first, then write it. Use the Writer's checklist to check your work: a capital letter at the start, finger spaces, and a full stop at the end. If you feel stuck, press Support — it gives you extra help. If it feels easy, press Challenge — it gives you a little more to do. I expect one sentence that makes sense and uses a farm word. Step 4. Press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved, so nothing is lost. You can come back later and make it even better. Then go to the next task and do the same three things: read it, look at the model, write and submit. Do all six tasks, one after another. Task 2 is tracing cow and hen — make the animal sound as you finish each word. Task 3 is matching duck, goat and sheep to their pictures, then copying the one that can swim. Task 4 is labelling your drawing with egg and field, with a little arrow to each place. Task 5 is finishing "First ___, then ___" about the hens. Task 6 is writing "I can see a ___" and counting that animal. Step 5. Now look at the bottom of the page. There is a slide deck called Plan, write and improve, with one task on each slide. Press Start. Write your sentences in the box — again, at least eight words. Press Submit this draft. Then press the arrow to go to the next task. Keep going until the slides run out. I expect you to say each sentence out loud before you write it. You will know the page is finished when all six tasks show your writing, you have pressed Submit this draft each time, and the slides at the bottom have no more arrows to press. Ready? Start with Step 1 and tell me when your first task is open. 🌾

activities.label: Activities
activities.text: Hello! Today we are on the Activities page for our farm unit. This page is where you play, colour, move and talk about the farm. We do it so the farm words come out of your mouth easily — cow, hen, barn, moo, baa. By the end you can name farm animals, make their sounds, and say "I can see a ___." You need crayons, paper, your voice, and a grown-up nearby if one is there. Here is what I expect from you today. Say every word out loud, not just in your head. Try even when you are not sure. Mistakes are how we learn. Step 1. Look at the top of the page. There are 6 activities. Read the words for the first one, and press Hear the instructions to listen. Listen all the way to the end, then say back what you must do. That is how I know you are ready. Step 2. Now do the activity. Activity 1 asks you to colour the farm animals: pig pink, cow brown, chick yellow, duck white. Point to each one and say its name out loud. Some activities have a box — write your answer in the box. Short is fine, even one word. Step 3. When you finish an activity, press Mark complete under it. Only press it after you really did the activity, not before. Then go to the next one and do the same: read, press Hear the instructions, do it, press Mark complete. Step 4. Here is what is coming in the other activities, so you know. Activity 2 is drawing your favourite farm animal and saying: This is a ___. It says ___. It has ___ legs. Activity 3 is matching each animal to its sound — say every sound nice and loud. Activity 4 is moving: waddle like a duck, hop like a lamb, peck like a hen, and name each one. Step 5. Activity 5 is finding things in the farm picture: barn, tractor, field, pond. Say "I can see a ___" for each one you find. Activity 6 is growing a bean in a cup with cotton wool and a little water. Look at it every day and tell a grown-up one thing that changed, or draw it. Step 6. Now scroll down to the bottom of the page. There is a slide deck called Learn by doing, with one activity on each slide. Press Start on the first slide. Do that activity, then press Mark complete. Step 7. Press the arrow to go to the next slide. Do that one too, then press Mark complete again. Keep going, slide by slide. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 8. On the last slide, press Finish activities. That tells the page you finished the whole deck. Well done for going all the way to the end! Step 9. Last of all, press Finish activities at the bottom of the page. Do this only when all 6 activities say complete and the slides are done. You will know the page is finished when every activity has Mark complete pressed, and you have pressed Finish activities at the bottom. Ready? Start with Step 1, and tell me when Activity 1 is coloured. 🐮

games.label: Games
games.text:
Hello! Today we are playing the farm games. Games are how we practise our new words in a fun way. You will name farm animals, make their sounds, and spot farm things like the barn and the tractor. All you need is your eyes, your ears, and your voice. Let's start! Here is what I expect from you: say each word out loud as you play, take your time, and use a hint if you get stuck. Hints are helpers, not cheating. Step 1. Look at the Games page. Press one game to open it. Any game is fine — pick the one that looks fun. Play it right to the end. You earn stars and XP for the answers you know. If a question is hard, press the hint button, or try again. I want to hear you say the word out loud each time, like "cow" or "moo". Step 2. When that game finishes, go back and play the next game. Play every game at least once. Don't rush — read or listen to each question twice before you choose. Good playing looks like this: you think, you say the word, then you press. Step 3. Now play your favourite games again to get more stars. The more you play, the more the words stick in your head. Try to beat your own score. If you get one wrong, that is fine — mistakes are how we learn. Step 4. When you have played them all, press the button that says I have played them all. Only press it after every game has been played once. That tells the page you are done. You will know the page is finished when you press I have played them all — or, if you get all the stars in every game, the page finishes by itself. 🌟

Go and press your first game now, then come back and tell me which one you played!

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text: Hello, my friend! Today is your farm quiz. This is where you show what you learned about cows, hens, sounds and seeds. I will not tell you any answers — but I know you can do this. You just need your eyes, your thinking and a calm, slow brain. Take your time — there's no rush. Here is what we will do, step by step. Step 1: There are ten questions. Read each question twice before you choose. Look at all four choices, then pick the one that feels right. If a question asks about a sound, say the sound softly in your head — moo, baa, quack, cluck — and see which animal makes it. If it asks about a doing word, look for the word with -ing on the end, like running or eating. Click the one answer you choose, then move to the next question. I expect you to try every question, even the tricky ones. Guessing your best guess is much better than skipping. Step 2: When you finish the last question, your score will show on the screen. You pass when you get more than half right. That means six or more out of ten. Look at your score and tell me how you did — I would love to hear! Then look at the ones you got wrong and think, "Ooh, why was that?" Mistakes are how we learn. Step 3: If your score is not high enough, press Try again and do the quiz one more time. That is not a sad thing — it is practice, and practice makes us strong. Go slower this time and read each question twice. When your score is good, press Continue to go to My progress. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Continue and you can see My progress. Then come back and tell me your score, and we can practise the words that felt hard. Good luck — off you go! 🐄🐔

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text: Hello! Today we are going to read a book together on the Books page. This is our reading time for Unit 5, On the Farm. We read so we can meet farm words like cow, hen, barn and seed, and hear how a story sounds in English. By the end, you will have read one whole book and you will be able to tell me one thing that happened in it. You need your eyes, your ears, and your voice. Ready? Here are the three steps. 1. Choose a book from the shelf. Look at the shelf on your screen. Look at the covers and pick one that you like. If you see "Amal and the Little Hen", that is our farm story — a lovely one to choose. Tap the book to open it. I expect you to pick one book and open it, not open lots of books at once. 2. Read it page by page. Press the arrow button to go to the next page, and the other arrow to go back. Say the words out loud if you can, or listen carefully as they are read. If your book plays as a video, just watch and listen. Tap the pictures too — they make sounds! When you tap a cow, listen for "moo". I expect you to say or copy at least a few words out loud, and to take your time. There is no rush. 3. Finish the book. Keep going with the arrows, or keep watching, until you reach the very last page. Do not stop in the middle. On the last page you will see a button that says Finish book. Press Finish book. I expect you to press it only when you have truly reached the end. You will know the page is done when you have pressed Finish book on the last page. One book is enough to finish this page — but if you loved it, you can go back to the shelf and read another one. Reading more is always a happy extra! When you press Finish book, come and tell me: what was your favourite part? I would love to hear it.

overview.label: Overview
overview.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 6: My Five Senses. This page is called Overview. Overview means "a first look". It tells you what you will learn before you begin. We do this so your brain knows what is coming — just like looking at a map before a trip. You need your eyes, your ears, and your voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. There are three steps on this page. Here they all are. Step 1. Read the unit preview on this page. It is the short part that tells you what you will learn. If you see a Listen button, press it and follow the words with your finger as you hear them. I expect you to hear or read the five senses: see, hear, smell, taste and touch. Try saying them out loud with me: see, hear, smell, taste, touch! Step 2. Read the four steps under How to learn. This is the plan for every page in this unit. Read them slowly, one at a time. I expect you to know one thing after this: what you will do first. If a grown-up is near, tell them, "First I learn the words." That shows you understood. Step 3. Press the button that says I have previewed this unit. Only press it after you have really looked at the preview — that button is your promise that you did. Then press Open vocabulary. That takes you to the first page, where we meet our new words. You will know this page is finished when you have pressed I have previewed this unit and then Open vocabulary, and the new word page opens. Take your time — there's no rush. When you get to the vocabulary page, come and tell me, and we will learn three new words together! 😊

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text:
Hello! Today we are learning the words for Unit 6, My Five Senses. These are words like see, hear, nose, soft and sweeter. We learn them so you can talk about what you see, hear, smell, taste and touch. There are 57 words, and you will do the same easy steps for each one. You need your voice, your eyes, and your fingers for typing. Say every word out loud — that is how words stick. 1. Look at the word list on the left side. Press one word. A card opens for that word. Start with the first word at the top. I expect you to work through every word, one at a time — not all at once. Take your time. 2. On the card, press Hear it. Listen carefully. Now say the word out loud yourself, in a big clear voice. Then press Again and say it one more time. I expect to hear your voice, not just your thinking. Say it with me, slowly. 3. Now read the Meaning on the card. Press the little speaker next to it to hear it read to you. Then say what the word means in your own words. It does not have to match exactly. A good answer is a short one, like "soft means it feels nice and gentle to touch."

4. Next is In a sentence. Read each practice sentence. Press Hear sentence to listen to it. Use the arrows to go through every sentence, not just the first one. Then pick one sentence and read it out loud yourself. I expect clear reading, one word at a time if you need to. 5. Now look at Spelling on the card. Look at the letters. Say them one by one, like s... o... f... t. Then say the whole word again: soft. Listen carefully, then spell it for me letter by letter. 6. Now it is your turn to write. Find the box that says Write your own sentence. The grey words give you a start. Type a sentence using the word. Then press Check sentence. Read what the checker tells you and fix anything it points out. I expect a real sentence about your own life, like "I can hear my mother." A capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end, please. 7. When you can say the word, tell me its meaning, and you have written your sentence, press I know this word. The word gets a LEARNED tag in the list. Only press it when all three are done. That tag means you really know it. 8. Now press the next word in the list. Do all the same steps again: Hear it, Again, Meaning, In a sentence, Spelling, Write your own sentence, Check sentence, I know this word. Do a few words, then have a little break. Short and happy is best. 9. Under the word list there is a deck of slides with the same words, one word on each slide. If you like, learn there instead. Press the Start button on the first slide, which says Say the words. On each slide press Hear it and Again, press Meaning to hear the meaning, read the sentences and press Hear sentence, look at the Spelling line, open Write your own sentence and press Check sentence, then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right for the next slide. The dots under the slide show where you are. On the last slide, when every word is marked, press the finish button. Cards or slides — both are fine. The words are the same. You will know the page is finished when every word in the list has a LEARNED tag next to it, and no word is left plain. That is 57 words said, understood and used by you. Ready? Press the first word in the list and press Hear it. Tell me which word you chose, and I will listen with you. 😊

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text:
Hello! Today we start Unit 6, My Five Senses. This page is our video lesson. You will watch a teacher, listen to new words, and say them out loud with her. By the end, you will know the five senses: see, hear, smell, taste and touch. You need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a quiet space. There are three steps. Let's begin! 1. Press play on the video and watch it right to the end. Sit still and look at the screen. Words will pop up at the bottom — these are called captions. Try to read them as you listen. I expect you to watch the whole video, not stop halfway. If a bit is tricky, you can watch it again. 2. Say the words out loud with the teacher in the video. When she says "eyes", you say "eyes" too! Say it big and clear, like you are talking to a friend across the room. I expect to hear your voice, not just your head thinking. Point to your eyes, your ears and your nose as you say them — that helps the words stick. 3. When the video has finished, press the button under it to go on to Vocabulary. Only press it after the video is really over. That button saves your work and takes you to our next page, where we learn the words more slowly. You will know this page is finished when the video has ended, you have said the words out loud, and you have pressed the button to go to Vocabulary. Then the new page will open — that means you did it! 🌟

Press play now, and come and tell me one word you heard.

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text: Hello! Today we are on the Reading and story page of Unit 6, My Five Senses. On this page there are three texts on the reading shelf. One is our story, Amal at the Market. One is our talk lines. One is our rhyme and song. We read them so we can meet our new words — see, hear, smell, taste, touch — and hear how they sound in real sentences. What I expect from you: a good try at reading out loud, a pointing finger following the words, and your voice joining in. You need your eyes, your ears, your finger, and a grown-up nearby if one is there. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 1. Read the text you can see on the screen. Read it slowly, out loud if you can. Point to each word with your finger as you say it. If a word is hard, say the first sound and try. I expect you to read to the end, not to be perfect. Step 2. Now press Prepare audio. Wait a moment. Then press the play button. Listen carefully and follow the words with your finger. Try to whisper along with the voice. This helps your ears and your eyes work together. Step 3. Some texts are for listening first. If yours is one, listen all the way through, then read it along with the voice. Read the story Amal at the Market very carefully. That is the one the Comprehension questions will ask you about later. Step 4. Press Next text to go to the next one. Press Previous text if you want to go back. Read every one of the three texts. Do not skip any. In the rhyme, say the words out loud and point to your eyes, ears, nose and mouth. Step 5. Look under the reading. There is a deck of slides with the same text, one page at a time. On the first slide, press Start where it says Read the story. On each page, read it, or press the speaker to listen. Then press the arrow to turn the page. On the last page, press I have read this text. Step 6. When all three texts are read, press Finished reading. That tells the page you are done. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I have read this text on the last slide, and then pressed Finished reading. Then come back and tell me one thing Amal smelled at the market. Good luck — I know you can do this!

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Comprehension page. Comprehension means showing what you understood from our story, "Amal at the Market", and our talk lines. We do this so the story stays in your head, and so you can say your ideas in full sentences. By the end you will have answered 12 questions and talked about the story out loud. You need your eyes to read, a grown-up nearby to help read the words, and your voice. Let's look at that together. Here is what I expect from you: try every question by yourself first, write in a full sentence like "Amal went with her grandmother," and start with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Take your time — there's no rush. There are 5 steps. Here they are. Step 1. Look at the first question on the page. Read it, or ask your grown-up to read it to you. Then think about our story for a moment. Ask yourself: what happened in that part? Picture Amal at the busy market in your head before you write anything. Step 2. Click inside the answer box and type your answer in a full sentence. Not just one word — a whole sentence, please. If the question asks "Who took Amal to the market?", write "Amal went to the market with her grandmother." Say it out loud first, then write it. That is a good answer. Step 3. Now press Check guidance. This shows you a good answer so you can compare it with yours. If your box is empty, the page will ask you to write first, so always write before you press it. Do not worry if your words are different from the good answer — if your idea is the same, you got it! Do steps 1, 2 and 3 for all 12 questions, one at a time. Step 4. Now go down to the slides at the bottom, called "Think about the story". Press Start. One question shows on each slide. Say your answer out loud in a full sentence, then press Check guidance to see a good answer. Press the arrow to go to the next question. Keep going until the last slide, then press Finish comprehension there. Speaking out loud is real practice, so use a nice clear voice. Step 5. Last, go to the bottom of the page and press Finish comprehension. Only press it when all 12 boxes have your writing in them and the slides are done. That button tells the page you have finished your work. You will know the page is finished when every question has your sentence in it, you have pressed Check guidance on each one, the slides are all done, and you have pressed Finish comprehension at the bottom. Then you are all done! Start with question one now, and tell me your sentence — I would love to hear it. 😊

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Grammar page of Unit 6, My Five Senses. On this page you learn six little sentence patterns, like "I can see with my eyes" and "This is softer than that." A pattern is a sentence shape you can use again and again with new words. We do this so you can talk about what you see, hear, smell, taste and touch. You need your voice, your ears, and your fingers for pointing. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. Here is what I expect from you today: say every sentence out loud in a clear voice, point to the body part when you say it, and take your time. Talking is the work here, not writing. Step 1 — Read the six lessons. Start at the first lesson. Read the rule and look at the example sentence. Then press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear it read to you. Listen carefully to how the words sound. I expect you to listen to each lesson at least once before you move on. Step 2 — Say the examples out loud. After you hear a sentence, say it back yourself. Say it slowly and clearly, like this: "I can see with my eyes." Touch the body part as you say it, so your eyes, ears, nose, tongue and hands all get a turn. A good try is a whole sentence, not just one word. Step 3 — Do the practice in every lesson. Under each lesson, press Show practice. Try the practice sentences out loud first. Then press Hear the practice to check how they should sound. If yours sounded a bit different, say it once more. Do this for all six lessons, one at a time, so nobody gets left out. Step 4 — Say the patterns in the slides. Scroll down to the slides at the bottom called Say the patterns. Press Start. Each slide shows one pattern. Say the pattern out loud, try the practice on that slide, then press the speaker to hear it. Move to the next slide and do the same. Keep going all the way to the last slide. I expect a big, clear voice on every slide. Step 5 — Finish the page. When all six lessons and all the slides are done, press the button at the bottom that says I practised all the lessons. Only press it after you really did them all, because that button is your record of your work. You will know the page is finished when every lesson has been read and practised, the slides have gone all the way to the last one, and the I practised all the lessons button has been pressed. Now go to Lesson 1 and press the speaker. Come back and tell me when Step 1 is done, and I will check it with you. Take your time — there's no rush.

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text: Hello! Today I am your speaking teacher, and this page is all about your voice. On this page you will practise talking about your five senses. You will say sentences like "I can see with my eyes" and "This is softer than that." We practise out loud because talking makes the words stick in your mouth and in your memory. You need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby to help with the buttons. Sit up tall and take a big breath — here we go! 1. Listen to the model. In each practice, press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear the sentence. Listen two times. The first time, just listen. The second time, watch how the words go up and down. I expect you to be quiet and listen carefully, not to talk yet. 2. Say it yourself, out loud. After listening twice, say the whole sentence in a big, clear voice. Say every word, like "I can hear with my ears." A good try is loud enough for someone in the room to hear you. Do not whisper, and do not rush. 3. Record your voice. Press the microphone button. Say your sentence clearly. Then press the microphone again to stop. I expect one clear sentence, with a tiny pause before you start so your first word is not cut off. 4. Listen to yourself. Press play and listen to your own recording. Ask yourself: can I hear every word? This is the fun part — you get to be the teacher of your own voice. 5. Submit for the check. Press Submit for pronunciation check. This button wakes up after you have listened back to yourself. Read what the checker tells you, or ask a grown-up to read it to you. 6. Try again if you want to. If the checker says a word was not clear, say that word slowly, then record again. Mistakes are how we learn. Do steps 1 to 6 for every one of the six practices. 7. Now the slides at the bottom. Under the practices there is a deck called Use your voice, with one practice on each slide. Press Start to begin. 8. On each slide, press Hear model first. Listen, then say it yourself out loud. Then press Record, say your sentence, and press Submit. Then press the arrow to go to the next practice. Keep going until you have done every slide. 9. Press the Finish speaking practices button at the bottom of the page. Only press it when you have finished all six practices and all the slides. You will know the page is done when every practice has your recording, you have pressed Submit each time, all the slides are finished, and you have pressed Finish speaking practices. Take your time — there's no rush. Come back and tell me when you finish practice one, and I will listen to how it went! 🌟

writing.label: Writing
writing.text: Hello! Today I am your writing teacher for our unit, My Five Senses. On this page you will write about your senses. You will use words like eyes, ears, soft and sweet. Writing helps you show what you know. You need a pencil, paper for drawing, and your voice for saying words out loud first. Take your time — there's no rush. Here is what I expect from you. Say your sentence out loud first. Then write it. Start with a big capital letter and finish with a full stop. Try your best letters. Mistakes are how we learn. Here are all the steps. 1. Look at the list of writing tasks. There are 6 of them. Click the first one to open it. Read the task with a grown-up if one is near you. If you see a speaker, press Hear the task and listen carefully. I expect you to know what the task is asking before you write. 2. Press View model text. This shows you a good example, like "I can see with my eyes." Read it slowly. Look at the capital letter at the start and the full stop at the end. I expect you to copy the shape of that sentence, but use your own idea. 3. Now write in the big box. Write at least eight words. That is about one good sentence, or two short ones. Use the Writer's checklist to check your work. If you feel stuck, press Support for extra help. If it feels easy, press Challenge and add one more sentence. I expect a capital letter, a full stop, and words I can read. 4. Press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved. You can come back later and make it even better. Then go back to the list and do the next task, one after another, until all 6 are done. I expect you to finish every task, not just one. 5. Now look at the slides at the bottom of the page. This deck is called Plan, write and improve. There is one task on each slide. Press Start. Write your sentences in the box — at least eight words again. Press Submit this draft. Then press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going until the last slide. You will know the page is finished when all 6 writing tasks are submitted and every slide in the deck is submitted too. When you are ready, tell me which task you picked first, and I will help you with it. 😊

activities.label: Activities
activities.text:
Hello! Today we are on the Activities page for our unit, My Five Senses. These activities let you use your senses for real. You will look, listen, smell, touch and taste. You will also say sentences like "I can see with my eyes" and "It is soft." By the end, you will know all five senses and the body parts we use. You will need a pencil, some crayons, and a grown-up nearby to help. Here is everything you will do, step by step. Step 1. Look at the first activity on the page. Press Hear the instructions and listen carefully. Listen all the way to the end, even if you think you know it. I expect you to listen first, then say the instruction back in your own words. That is how good learners start. Step 2. Now do the activity. Some activities ask you to write in the box. Write your answer in the box in your best letters, and say it out loud before you write it. Short is fine — one or two words, or one sentence. I expect a real try, not a perfect one. Mistakes are how we learn. Step 3. When you have finished that activity, press Mark complete under it. Only press it after you have really done the activity. Then move to the next one and do the same: press Hear the instructions, do it, press Mark complete. There are 6 activities in all, so you will do this six times. Step 4. Scroll down to the bottom of the page. There is a slide deck called Learn by doing, with one activity on each slide. Press Start. Do the activity on that slide, then press Mark complete. Then press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going, slide by slide. On the very last slide, press Finish activities. I expect you to do each slide properly, not skip ahead with the arrow. Step 5. Last of all, press Finish activities at the bottom of the page. Press it only when every activity has its Mark complete pressed. That tells the page you are all done. How will you know the page is finished? Every activity will show as complete, and you will have pressed Finish activities at the bottom. 🌟

Now go and press Hear the instructions on activity 1. Come back and tell me what it asks you to do!

games.label: Games
games.text: Hello! Today we are going to play the games on this page. Games are how we practise our five senses words in a fun way. You will name the senses, match body parts, use words like soft, loud and sweet, and compare things with words like taller and sweeter. All you need is your eyes, your ears, your finger to tap, and your happy voice. A grown-up can sit beside you if one is nearby. Here is what we will do. 1. Press a game to open it. Look at the games on your screen and choose one you like. Tap it with your finger to start. Read or listen to the question, then choose your answer. If you feel stuck, press the hint — hints are there to help you, and using one is a smart thing to do. If you get one wrong, try again. You earn stars and XP for what you know. I expect you to try every question, even the tricky ones. Mistakes are how we learn. 2. Play every game at least once. When one game finishes, go back and press the next game. Keep going until you have opened and played them all. Say the words out loud as you play — "I can see with my eyes", "It is soft", "This is sweeter than that". Saying them helps you remember them. If you want more stars, press a game again and play it a second time. I expect you to finish every game, not just your favourite one. 3. When you have played them all, press I have played them all. This is the button that tells the page you are done. Only press it after you have really played each game once. If you get every game perfect, the page will finish all by itself — you will not need to press anything. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I have played them all, or when the page finishes by itself after you master every game. Then your stars are saved and your work is counted. Off you go — start with step one and press a game. Tell me which game you chose, and how it went. Take your time — there's no rush.

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text: Hello! Today is your checkpoint quiz for My Five Senses. A quiz is a little check to see what you remember. We do it so you can feel proud of all the sense words you learned — see, hear, smell, taste and touch. You need your eyes, your thinking brain, and a grown-up nearby if you want one. I will not tell you answers, but I will help you think. Here are all the steps. 1. Read each question, then choose one answer. There are 10 questions. Look at the question and say it out loud if that helps. Then look at all four choices before you tap one. To think it out, ask yourself: which body part is doing the work? Eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, tongue tastes, hands touch. For describing words, ask: is this a sound, a taste, or a feel? For comparing, look for the little word "than" — that word means two things are being compared. I expect you to try every question, even the tricky ones. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Finish all 10, then look at your score. When you answer the last question, the page shows your score. More than half right means you passed — that is 6 or more out of 10. I expect you to read your score and tell me how you did. Then we can talk about which questions felt hard. 3. If your score is not high enough, press Try again. That button lets you do the quiz once more. Trying again is not a bad thing — it is how we get stronger. Before you start again, say the five senses out loud with me: see, hear, smell, taste, touch. Mistakes are how we learn. 4. When you are happy with your score, press Continue. That takes you to My progress, where you can see your work. I expect you to press it yourself, because the page only knows you are done when you press. You will know the page is finished when you have answered all 10 questions, seen your score, and pressed Continue to reach My progress. Ready? Here comes question one — read it twice, then choose. Tell me your answer and I will help you check your thinking.

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this is our Books page. On this page you read a story all by yourself. Our unit is My Five Senses, so listen out for words like see, hear, smell, taste and touch. Reading a story helps those words stick in your head. By the end you will have read one whole book and pressed Finish book. You need your eyes, your ears, and a quiet spot. If a grown-up is near, they can sit with you. Here are our three steps. 1. Choose a book from the shelf. Look at the shelf on your screen. Look at the covers and pick one you like. Tap the book you want, and it will open. I expect you to choose with your eyes first — look, then tap. Any book is a good choice. 2. Read the book page by page. Press the arrow button to go to the next page. Read the words slowly, out loud if you can. Then tap the pictures. Some pictures make a sound! That is your ears doing the work. If the book plays like a video, just watch and listen carefully. I expect you to look at every page, not rush. Take your time — there's no rush. 3. Go right to the end, then press Finish book. Keep pressing the arrow until you reach the last page. On the last page you will see the button Finish book. Press it. I expect you to finish the whole story before you press it — no skipping to the end! You will know the page is done when you have pressed Finish book. One book finishes this page. If you loved it, you may go back to the shelf and read another one. Now go and choose your book. When you have chosen, come and tell me which one you picked, and one thing you can see on the cover.

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text:
Hello! Today we start Unit 7. It is called "Let's Go!"

This page is our video lesson. You will watch a teacher on the screen. She will show you words for how we travel — walk, bus, car, bicycle and boat. By the end, you will be able to say those words and tell me how you go to school. You need two things: your ears for listening, and your voice for talking. That is all! There are three steps. Here they are. Step 1. Press the play button on the video. Then watch it all the way to the end. Sit still and listen carefully. Little words will appear at the bottom of the video — these are called captions. Try to look at them as you listen. I expect you to watch the whole video without stopping. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 2. Say the words out loud with the teacher in the video. When she says "bus", you say "bus" too! When she says a whole sentence like "I go by car", you say it too. Say it in a big, happy voice. I expect to hear your voice, not just the video's voice. Even if a word feels hard, try it — trying is what makes it easy later. Step 3. When the video has finished, look under the video. There is a button there to go on to Vocabulary. Press it. That takes you to the next page, where we meet the travel words more closely. I expect you to press it only after the video is really finished, not in the middle. You will know this page is finished when the video has ended, you have said the words out loud, and you have pressed the button to go to Vocabulary. Now, off you go — press play! Tell me when you have watched it, and I will ask you one little question about the video. 🚌

overview.label: Overview
overview.text:
Hello! Today we start Unit 7. It is called "Let's Go!"

This page is the Overview. Overview means a little look at everything before we begin. It is like peeking at the road before we take a trip. Why do we do it? Because it helps your brain get ready. When you know what is coming, the words are easier to learn. What I expect from you: eyes on the words, ears listening, and your voice saying words out loud. You do not need a pencil for this page. There are three small steps. Here they are. Step 1: Read the unit preview at the top of this page. It tells you what you will learn about travelling — walk, bus, car, bicycle and boat. If you see a Listen button, press it and follow the words with your finger as they are read. Do it well by saying one or two travel words out loud after you read. I expect you to find at least one way to travel that YOU use, like walking or the bus. Step 2: Read the four steps under How to learn. These four steps show how you will work on every page of this unit. Take them slowly, one line at a time, and ask your grown-up to read any tricky word for you. I expect you to know one thing you will do in this unit — for example, listen to a story, or sing a song about a bus. Step 3: Press the button that says I have previewed this unit. That button tells the page, "Yes, I looked!" Then press Open vocabulary. That takes you to the first page, where we meet our new travel words together. I expect you to press them in that order — the first one, then the second one. How will you know this page is finished? You have read the preview, you have read the four How to learn steps, and you have pressed I have previewed this unit and then Open vocabulary. When the vocabulary page opens, this page is done. Before you go — tell me one way YOU travel. Do you walk, or go by bus, or by car? 🚌

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text: Hello! Today we are on our reading shelf for Unit 7, Let's Go! This page has three texts about travelling. One is our story, Amal's Big Bus Ride. One is talking lines to say out loud. One is our bus song and rhyme. Reading them helps you hear travel words like bus, wheels, fast and slow, and get ready for the questions later. You need your eyes, your finger, your voice, and your listening ears. Let's go! Here are your six steps. 1. Read the text on the screen slowly. Look at the first text. Read it out loud if you can, one line at a time. Point at each word with your finger as you say it. It is okay to go slowly. I expect you to try every word, even the tricky ones. 2. Listen to it too. Press Prepare audio. Wait a little moment. Then press the play button. Follow the words with your finger while the voice reads.
