I expect your finger to move along with the voice, like a little train on a track. 3. Read our story with extra care. If a text is a listening text, listen first, then read along. Amal's Big Bus Ride is our unit story, and the Comprehension questions come from it. So read that one carefully. I expect you to remember the colour of the bus and how Amal travelled first. 4. Move to the next text. Press Next text to go forward. Press Previous text to go back. Read every text, not just one. I expect you to read all three before you stop. 5. Do the slides at the bottom. Under the reading there is a deck of slides with the same text, one page at a time. On the first slide, press Start. On each page, read it, or press the speaker to listen. Then press the arrow to turn the page. On the last page, press I have read this text. I expect you to read or listen to every page, not skip ahead. 6. Finish the page. When you have read all three texts, press Finished reading. That tells the page you are done. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I have read this text on the slides and then pressed Finished reading. That is when your reading work is saved. Take your time — there's no rush. Come and tell me when you finish the first text, and tell me one thing you saw in the story!

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Vocabulary page of Unit 7, Let's Go! Here is what we are doing. This page has 57 travel words, like bus, boat and wheels. You will learn them one word at a time: hear it, say it, know what it means, and use it in your own sentence. By the end, you will be able to talk about how you travel in English. You need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby to help you type. Say every word out loud — that is how words stick! Here are all the steps. 1. Open a word. Look at the word list on the left side. Press one word. A card opens up. Start with the first word and work down the list. I expect you to do one word at a time, not jump around. 2. Hear it and Again. Press Hear it and listen carefully. Now say the word out loud, just like you heard it. Then press Again and say it one more time. Out loud, please — not quietly in your head! 3. Meaning. Read the meaning on the card. Press the little speaker next to it to hear it read to you. Now tell me what the word means in your own words. It does not have to be perfect. "A bus is a big car for lots of people" is a lovely answer. 4. In a sentence. Read each practice sentence on the card. Press Hear sentence to listen to it. Use the arrows to see every sentence. Then pick one you like and read it out loud yourself, nice and clear. 5. Spelling. Look at the letters on the card. Say each letter one by one, slowly: b... u... s. Then say the whole word again. This helps your eyes and your mouth learn together. 6. Write your own sentence. Find the box that says Write your own sentence. Type a sentence with your word in it. The grey words give you a start, so you are not alone. Then press Check sentence. Read what it tells you, and fix anything it points out. I expect one sentence about your real life, like "I go by bus."

7. I know this word. When you can say the word, tell the meaning, and you have written your sentence, press I know this word. The word gets a LEARNED tag in the list. That is your gold star! 8. Next word. Press the next word in the list. Do steps 2 to 7 again for that word. Take your time — there's no rush. Little bits every day work best. 9. The slides at the bottom. Under the word list there is a deck of slides with the same words, one word on each slide. Press the Start button on the first slide, called Say the words. On each slide, press Hear it and Again to listen and say the word, press Meaning to hear what it means, read the sentences and press Hear sentence, look at the Spelling line, open Write your own sentence and type yours, press Check sentence, then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right for the next slide. The little dots under the slide show where you are. On the last slide, when every word is marked, press the finish button. The cards at the top and the slides at the bottom teach the same words — you may choose either one. How will you know the page is finished? Look at your word list. When every single word has a LEARNED tag, you are done. If you are using the slides, you are done when you press the finish button on the last slide. Ready? Press your first word and begin with step 2. Tell me when you have said your first word out loud, and I will cheer you on! 🚌

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Hello! Today we are doing Comprehension on this page. Comprehension means showing that you understand the story. You read the story about Amal and her big bus ride. Now you answer questions about it. This helps you remember the story and say it in your own words. You need your reading page, your eyes, your voice, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. Here is the whole page, step by step. 1. There are 12 questions about the texts you read. Read the first question slowly. Read it twice. Then think about the story in your head. Ask yourself: what happened in that part? I expect you to think first, before you type. 2. Type your answer in the box in a full sentence. A full sentence means the whole idea, not just one word. For example, if I asked "Who did Amal go to see?", a good answer is "Amal went to see her grandmother." Start with a big letter and end with a full stop. I expect one clear sentence in your own words. 3. Press Check guidance. This shows you a good answer. Read it and compare it with yours. If your box is empty, the page will ask you to write first, so always type something before you press. Do this for every one of the 12 questions. Your answer does not have to match word for word. I expect the same idea in your words. 4. Now look at the slides at the bottom. This deck is called Think about the story, with one question on each slide. Press Start. Read the question and say your answer out loud in a big, clear voice. Then press Check guidance to see a good answer. Press the arrow to go to the next question. Keep going until the last slide, then press Finish comprehension on that slide. I expect you to speak, not just think. 5. When every question is done, press Finish comprehension at the bottom of the page. Only press it when all 12 boxes have your writing in them and the slides are done. That button saves your work, so it must be you who presses it. You will know the page is finished when all 12 boxes are full, the slides say you are done, and you have pressed Finish comprehension. Ready? Start with question one, and tell me when you have typed your first answer. 😊

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text:
Hello! Today we are doing our Speaking page for Unit 7, Let's Go! 🚌

This page is all about talking. You will listen to a sentence, then say it out loud yourself. We do this so your mouth gets used to English words like bus, boat and road. By the end, you will be able to say how YOU travel, in a clear, happy voice. What you need: your voice, your ears, and a grown-up near you to help press the buttons. What I expect from you: say every sentence OUT LOUD, not in your head. Speak slowly and clearly. Try your best, even if it feels funny. Mistakes are how we learn. Here are all the steps. Step 1. There are 6 speaking practices on this page. Start with the first one. Press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear the model sentence. Listen two times. The first time, just listen. The second time, watch how the words sound. Then say the sentence out loud yourself. I expect a big, clear voice — not a whisper. Step 2. Now press the microphone button. Say your sentence, like "I go by bus." Then press the microphone again to stop. Say it right after you press, so the start of your sentence is not cut off. I expect one full sentence, not just one word. Step 3. Press play and listen to your own recording. Ask yourself: can I hear every word? Was I too fast? It is fun to hear your own voice! I expect you to really listen, all the way to the end. Step 4. Now press Submit for pronunciation check. This button only wakes up after you have listened back to yourself. Read what the checker tells you, or ask your grown-up to read it. If you want to do better, record again and submit again. Do this for all 6 practices, one at a time. Step 5. Under the practices there is a slide deck called Use your voice. It has one practice on each slide. Press Start. Then press Hear model and listen. Say it yourself out loud. Press Record, say your sentence, then press Submit. Press the arrow to go to the next practice. Keep going until you have done every slide. Step 6. When all the practices are done, press the Finish speaking practices button at the bottom of the page. That tells the page you have finished your talking work. How will you know the page is finished? All 6 practices have a recording from you, the slides are all done, and you have pressed Finish speaking practices. 🌟

Now start with practice 1. Press the speaker and listen twice. Tell me when you have said it out loud, and I will help you with the next bit.

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Grammar page in Unit 7, Let's Go! Here is what this page is. It has six little lessons. Each lesson teaches one talking pattern about travel, like "I go by bus." We do this so you can talk about how you go places, in real English, out loud. What I expect from you: use your VOICE. Say every example loudly and clearly. Put your own word in the gap. It is fine to say a word twice, or three times. Mistakes are how we learn. You will need your voice, a quiet spot, and your grown-up nearby if you have one. Here are the steps. Step 1. Look at the first lesson at the top. Press the speaker button, or press Replay, and listen. Read the rule and the examples with your eyes while you listen. Good listening means you hear every word before you speak. I expect you to press the speaker at least once for each of the six lessons. Step 2. Now say the examples out loud. Say them slowly, like the voice did. For lesson one you will say, "I go by bus." Add the action with your hands — hold a steering wheel, or pedal a bike. I expect a clear voice, not a whisper. Step 3. Under each lesson, press Show practice. Try the practice sentences yourself. Put your own true word in the gap, like "I go by car." Then press Hear the practice and check if yours sounded the same. Do this for every one of the six lessons, one lesson at a time. Do not rush to the next lesson until you have said the one you are on. Step 4. Here are the six patterns you will meet, so you know what is coming: I go by ___. It goes on the ___. I can see a / an ___. The ___ is fast. We are ___ing. First we ___, then we ___. Step 5. Now go to the bottom of the page. There is a slide deck called Say the patterns. Press Start. One pattern comes up on each slide. Say the pattern out loud, try the practice, then press the speaker to hear it. Then move to the next slide. I expect you to go all the way to the last slide. Step 6. When all six lessons and all the slides are done, press the button that says I practised all the lessons. That button is at the bottom of the page. How will you know the page is finished? You have pressed the speaker in all six lessons, said every pattern out loud, opened Show practice in all six, reached the last slide, and pressed I practised all the lessons. Take your time — there's no rush. Come back and tell me which pattern was your favourite, and I will practise it with you! 🚌

writing.label: Writing
writing.text: Hello! I am your teacher today, and this is our Writing page for Unit 7, Let's Go! Here is what we are doing. You will write little bits of English about how we travel: buses, cars, boats and journeys. Writing helps the words stick in your head and in your hand. By the end you will be able to write a short sentence like "I go by bus." You need a pencil, some paper for drawing, and your voice for saying the words out loud first. What I expect from you: say your idea out loud BEFORE you write it. Use the model to help you. Try your best letters. It is fine to ask a grown-up to help you type or spell. There are 5 steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Look at the list of 6 writing tasks. Press the first one to open it. Read the task, and if you see a speaker, press Hear the task and listen carefully. Do them in order, task 1 first. I expect you to know what the task asks before you write anything. Step 2. Press View model text. This shows you one good example, like "I go by bus." Read it out loud, or ask a grown-up to read it with you. Look at the capital letter at the start and the full stop at the end. I expect you to copy the SHAPE of the model, not the exact words. Step 3. Now write your own in the big box. Say your sentence out loud first, then write it. Try to make it eight words or more, like "I go to school by bus with Mum." Use the Writer's checklist to check your work. If you feel stuck, press Support for extra help. If it feels easy, press Challenge to do a bit more. I expect a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end. Step 4. Press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved, so it is safe. You can come back later and make it better. Then go to the next task and do Step 1, 2 and 3 again, until all 6 tasks are done. I expect you to finish all six, one after another. Take your time, there is no rush. Step 5. Scroll down to the slides at the bottom, called Plan, write and improve. There is one task on each slide. Press Start, say your idea out loud, then write your sentences in the box, at least eight words. Press Submit this draft, then press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going until the last slide. How will you know the page is finished? When all 6 writing tasks have a saved draft, and every slide in the deck has been submitted too. Then you have done the whole page. Tell me when you have opened task 1, and I will help you with it. 😊

games.label: Games
games.text:
Welcome to the Games page, my friend! This is the fun part of Unit 7, "Let's Go!". These games practise our travel words — bus, car, boat, bicycle, walk, train and plane. Playing helps the words stick in your head, so you can say them out loud without stopping to think. You need your eyes, your voice and a grown-up nearby to help you press things. Let's go! 🚌

Step 1: Press a game to open it. Any game you like! Then play it. Say each word out loud as you play — say "bus", say "boat". If you get stuck, use the hint button. If you get one wrong, press retry and go again. You earn stars and XP for what you know. I expect you to try, not to be perfect. Mistakes are how we learn. Step 2: Play every game at least once. Go back and press the next game, then the next, until you have opened them all. If a game was tricky, play it again. Playing again gives you more stars. I expect every game to have been played by you at least one time. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 3: When you have played them all, press the button that says "I have played them all". Only press it when it is true! If you master every single game, the page will finish all by itself, and you will not need to press anything. You will know the page is finished when the games are all played and the page shows you are done. Then come and tell me one thing: which game was your favourite? And can you say "I go by ___" with your own way of travelling? Great work today!

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text:
Hello! Today we are doing the Books page for our unit, Let's Go! This page is our story time. You pick a book, then you read it or watch it, right to the end. Stories help you hear our travel words again — bus, car, boat, walk, fast, slow. When you finish, you will know a story you can tell to your grown-up. You need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a comfy seat. Let's go! There are three steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Choose a book from the shelf. Look at the shelf on your screen. Look at the covers and the pictures. Pick one that looks fun to you. Tap that book to open it. I expect you to choose all by yourself — there is no wrong book. If you see one about buses, boats or bicycles, that fits our unit beautifully. Step 2. Read it page by page, or watch it. Press the arrow to go to the next page. If the book plays like a video, just sit still and watch. Try to say the words out loud with the book — reading aloud helps the words stick. Tap the pictures too! When you tap a picture, you hear its sound. I expect you to look at each picture and try to name one thing you see, like "I can see a bus."

Step 3. Go right to the end, then press Finish book. Keep pressing the arrow until you reach the last page. Do not stop in the middle — a story is best when we hear the ending! On the last page, press Finish book. I expect you to tell me one thing that happened in the story, in your own words. Just one sentence is perfect. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Finish book on the last page of one book. One book finishes this page. If you loved it, go back to the shelf and read another one — reading more is always a happy choice! Ready? Go and choose your book, then tell me which one you picked. 📚

activities.label: Activities
activities.text:
Hello! Today we are on the Activities page for our unit, Let's Go! Here is what this page is. It has six little activities about how we travel. You will colour, draw, match, move like a bus or a plane, point and say, and make a road sign. We do this because it helps you say the travel words out loud with your own voice and hands. By the end, you will be able to name ways to travel and say "I go to school by ___."

What you need: crayons or colouring pencils, paper, and your speaking voice. A grown-up nearby can help you read and cut. What I expect from you: try every activity, say the words out loud (not just in your head), and do your best. Neat is nice, but talking is the real work here. There are 5 steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Read the instructions for each activity. There are 6 activities on the page. Look at the first one, then press Hear the instructions to listen to the words. Listening while you look helps a lot. I expect you to listen right to the end before you start. Step 2. Do the activity. Some activities ask you to write your answer in the box. Say your answer out loud first, then write it in the box. Keep it short, like "bus" or "I go to school by car." Do the doing parts too: colour the bus yellow, wave your arms to fly, point and say "I can see a ___." I expect a real try on each one. Step 3. Press Mark complete under each activity when you have finished it. Only press it after you have really done that activity. That button tells the page, "I did this one!" I expect six Mark complete presses, one for each activity. Step 4. Go down to the slides at the bottom of the page. This part is called Learn by doing. There is one activity on each slide. Press Start, do the activity, then press Mark complete. Then press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going slide by slide. On the last slide, press Finish activities. I expect you to do every slide, not skip any. Step 5. Press Finish activities at the bottom of the page when everything is done. That is your big finish button for the whole page. How will you know the page is finished? Every activity has Mark complete pressed, all the slides are done, and you have pressed Finish activities at the bottom. Then you are all done! Now go and do Step 1. Come back and tell me when you have listened to the first activity, and I will help you with it. 🚌

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text: Hello! This is our Let's Go! checkpoint. That is a little quiz about travelling — buses, cars, boats, planes and staying safe. We do it to see which words you know really well. By the end, you will know what you can do all by yourself. You just need your eyes, your thinking brain, and a grown-up nearby if you want one. Here is our plan. There are three parts. 1. Answer the ten questions. Press the answer you think is right for each one. Read the question twice before you answer — the words tell you a lot. Ask yourself: does this thing go on the road, on the water, or in the sky? For the sentence questions, say each choice out loud and listen. The one that sounds right, like "I go by bus", is usually the good one. Take your time — there's no rush. I expect you to try every question, even the tricky ones. I really can't give quiz answers — but I promise you can get this. 2. Look at your score at the end. When you finish the last question, your score will show on the screen. More than half right means you passed. That is six or more out of ten. I expect you to read your score and tell me how you did. I would love to hear it! 3. If your score is not high enough, press Try again. Then do all ten questions one more time. This is a good thing, not a sad thing — mistakes are how we learn. Go a bit slower this time and think about where each vehicle goes. When your score is good, press Continue. That takes you to My progress. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Continue and you can see My progress. That means your work is saved. Now go and press your first answer — I am right here if you get stuck!

overview.label: Overview
overview.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher, and this is our Overview page. 💧

Overview means "a little look at everything first." It tells you what our new unit, Wonderful Water, is all about. We do this so your brain knows what is coming — like looking at a map before a trip. By the end of this page, you will know what you will learn, and how to work through each page. You need your eyes, your listening ears, and your voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. Here is what I expect from you today: look at the words, listen carefully, and say things out loud. That is all. There is no writing on this page. Step 1. Read the unit preview at the top of this page. It tells you what you will learn about water. If you see a Listen button, press it and follow the words with your finger as you hear them. Do it well by listening all the way to the end, without stopping. I expect you to point at the words and try to say one water word out loud, like "rain" or "water". Step 2. Read the four steps under How to learn. These four steps show how you will work on every page of this unit. Read them slowly, one at a time. Ask your grown-up to read them aloud if the words are hard. I expect you to be able to tell me one thing you will do in this unit — for example, "I will listen to a story."

Step 3. Now press the button that says I have previewed this unit. That tells the page you are ready. Then press Open vocabulary. That button takes you to our first learning page, where we meet our new words. I expect you to press them in that order: first I have previewed this unit, then Open vocabulary. You will know this page is finished when you have listened to the preview, read the four steps, pressed I have previewed this unit, and the vocabulary page opens on your screen. Great work today! Off you go and start with Step 1. 🌧️

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text:
Hello! Today we start Unit 8: Wonderful Water. 💧

This page is our video lesson. You watch, you listen, and you say the words out loud with the teacher. We do this so water words like rain, wet, dry, float and sink go into your ears first. Words go into your ears before they go into your mouth! You need three things: your eyes, your ears, and your voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. There are three steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Press the play button on the video and watch it all the way to the end. Sit still and look at the screen. Words will pop up at the bottom — these are the captions. Try to look at them as you listen. I expect you to watch the whole video, right to the last part, without stopping halfway. Step 2. Say the words out loud with the teacher in the video. When the teacher says "water", you say "water" too. When she says "It is rainy", you say "It is rainy". Say it in a big, brave voice, not a whisper. It is fine if a word feels tricky — just try. I expect to hear your voice on most of the words, not only your eyes watching. Step 3. When the video has finished, press the button under it to go on to Vocabulary. Do this only after the video is really over. That button takes you to the next part of our unit, where we meet the water words again more slowly. You will know this page is finished when the video has played to the end, you have said the words out loud, and you have pressed the button to go on to Vocabulary. That is the whole page done! Off you go — press play now. Then come back and tell me one water word you heard. 🌧️

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text: Hello! Today we are learning our Wonderful Water words. These are the words we need to talk about rain, wells, floating, and animals that live in water. When we finish, you will be able to say each word, know what it means, and use it in your own sentence. You need your voice, your eyes, and a grown-up nearby to help you read and type. Let's start! Here are all the steps. Do them one at a time, and take your time. 1. Look at the word list on the left of the page. Press one word. A card opens for that word. There are 55 words in the list. You will do one word at a time — no rushing. Start with the very first word. 2. On the card, press Hear it. Listen carefully. Now say the word out loud, just like you heard it. Then press Again and say it one more time. Say it with your mouth, not just in your head! I want to hear a nice clear voice. 3. Next, read the Meaning on the card. Press the little speaker beside it to hear the meaning read to you. Then tell me the meaning in your own words. It does not need to be perfect. If the word is "float", you might say "it stays on top of the water". That is a great answer. 4. Now look at In a sentence. Read each sentence, then press Hear sentence to listen to it. Press the arrows to see every sentence for that word. Then pick one sentence you like and read it out loud yourself. Nice and slow, like a storyteller. 5. Now look at the Spelling on the card. Look at the letters. Say them one by one, like this: w, a, t, e, r. Then say the whole word again: water. Saying the letters helps your eyes remember the word. 6. Now it is your turn to write. Find Write your own sentence and type a sentence with the word in the box. The grey words help you start. Keep it short and true, like "I drink water." Then press Check sentence. Read what the checker tells you, and fix anything it says. Start with a capital letter and finish with a full stop. 7. When you can say the word, know what it means, and have written your sentence, press I know this word. The word gets a LEARNED tag in the list. That tag means "I did it!" Only press it when you really can do all three things. 8. Now press the next word in the list and do the same steps again: Hear it, Again, Meaning, In a sentence, Spelling, Write your own sentence, Check sentence, I know this word. Keep going, one word at a time. If you feel tired, stop and come back later. That is fine. 9. Under the word list there are slides with the same words, one word on each slide. If you like slides better, press the Start button on the first slide, the one that says Say the words. On each slide, press Hear it and Again to say the word, press Meaning to hear what it means, read the sentences and press Hear sentence, look at the Spelling line, open Write your own sentence and press Check sentence, then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right to go to the next slide. The little dots under the slide show you where you are. On the last slide, when every word is marked, press the finish button. Cards or slides — both are good. The words are the same. You will know the page is finished when every word in the list has a LEARNED tag beside it, or when you press the finish button on the last slide. Ready? Press your first word and press Hear it. Tell me the word you chose and I will listen with you. 💧

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text:
Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Reading and story page of Unit 8, Wonderful Water. On this page there are three texts on the reading shelf: our story "The Well in the Village", the talking lines "Talk about Wonderful Water", and our rhyme with "Row, Row, Row Your Boat". We read them so your English gets stronger, so you learn water words like well, float and waste, and so you are ready for the questions later. You need your eyes, your finger, your voice, and a quiet spot. Here are all six steps. 1. Read the text on the screen slowly. Put your finger under the first word and move it along as you read. Read out loud if you can, even softly. It is fine to read slowly, and it is fine to stop and try a hard word again. I expect you to read every line, not just look at the pictures. 2. Now press Prepare audio, wait a moment, then press the play button. Listen while your finger follows the words. Try to whisper the words with the voice. I expect your finger and the voice to stay together — that is how your eyes learn each word. 3. If a text is a listening text, listen to it first, then read it. Our unit story is "The Well in the Village". That is the one the Comprehension questions ask about, so read it carefully and slowly. As you read, think about Amal, the well, and the day the rain came. I expect you to be able to tell me one thing that happened in the story. 4. Press Next text to go to the next one, and Previous text to go back. Read every text on the shelf, all three. Do not skip the rhyme — you can say it out loud and wiggle your fingers like rain. I expect you to visit each text and read it, one after another. 5. Look under the reading. There is a deck of slides with the same text, one page at a time. On the first slide press Start, called Read the story. On each page, read it yourself, or press the speaker to hear it. Then press the arrow to turn the page. On the last page, press I have read this text. I expect you to read every page before you press the arrow — no fast clicking! 6. When you have read all three texts and finished the slides, press Finished reading. That is your way of telling the page, "I did it."

You will know the page is finished when every text has been read, the slides show I have read this text, and you have pressed Finished reading. Take your time — there's no rush. When you finish, come and tell me your favourite part of the story! 💧

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Hello! Today we are doing Comprehension. That means we talk about the story we read, "The Well in the Village", and the talk lines about water. We do it so you can remember the story and say your ideas in a full sentence. You will need your reading page and your voice. By the end, you will be able to answer questions about water all by yourself. Here are the steps. 1. Look at the first question. There are 12 questions in all. Read it with a grown-up if one is near, or read it slowly out loud. Think about the story: who was in it, what happened, what water was used for. I expect you to think before you write — take your time, there's no rush. 2. Now type your answer in the box. Try to write a full sentence, not just one word. If the question asks "What did they carry?", write "They carried a pot," not just "pot." Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Say it out loud first, then write it — that always helps. 3. Press Check guidance. This shows you a good answer so you can compare it with yours. If your box is empty, the page will ask you to write first — so always write your own answer before you press it. Your answer does not have to match word for word. If it says the same idea, that's a win! Do steps 1, 2 and 3 for every one of the 12 questions. 4. Now scroll down to the slides at the bottom, called Think about the story. Press Start. One question shows on each slide. Say your answer out loud in a big, clear voice. Then press Check guidance to see a good answer, and press the arrow to go to the next question. Keep going, slide by slide. On the last slide, press Finish comprehension. 5. Last of all, press Finish comprehension at the bottom of the page. Only press it when all 12 boxes have your writing in them and you have said all the slide questions out loud. You will know the page is finished when every question box has your own sentence in it, you have pressed Check guidance for each one, and you have pressed Finish comprehension at the bottom. Then you are all done! Ready for question one? Tell me what you type, and I will look at it with you. 🙂

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Grammar page in our unit, Wonderful Water. On this page you learn six little talking patterns about water. Things like "I use water to drink," "It is rainy," and "Fish live in water." We do this so you can talk about water in real English, out loud, with a strong voice. You will need your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. Ready? Here are all the steps. Step 1. Look at the first grammar lesson. Read the rule and the little examples. Then press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear it read to you. Listen carefully to how the words sound. I expect you to listen right to the end before you move on. Step 2. Now say the examples out loud. Say them slowly and clearly, like this: "I use water to drink." Not a whisper — a nice big voice! I expect you to say each example at least one time. Saying it two times is even better. Step 3. Under the lesson, press Show practice. Try the practice sentences out loud. Then press Hear the practice to check how they sound. Did your voice sound like the audio? Good! Now do Step 1, Step 2 and Step 3 again for every lesson, until you finish all six. I expect you to try every lesson, even the tricky ones. Step 4. Scroll down to the slides at the bottom. This part is called Say the patterns. Press Start. On each slide there is one pattern. Say it out loud, try the practice, then press the speaker to hear it. Then go to the next slide. Keep going until you reach the very last slide. I expect you to speak on every single slide. Step 5. When all six lessons and all the slides are done, press the button that says I practised all the lessons. This tells the page you finished your work today. You will know the page is finished when every lesson is read and said, all the slides are done to the last one, and you have pressed I practised all the lessons. Take your time — there's no rush. Come and tell me when you finish Step 1, and I will help you with the rest! 💧

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text: Hello! Today we are on the Speaking page of Wonderful Water. This page is all about talking. You will listen to a sentence, then say it out loud with your own voice. Speaking out loud helps your mouth learn English words, so they come out easily. You need your voice, your ears, and a quiet spot. A grown-up can sit with you and help you press the buttons. What I expect from you: say every sentence out loud, not just in your head. Speak slowly and clearly, like you are telling a friend. It is fine if it is not perfect — trying is the win! Here is the whole page, step by step. 1. There are 6 speaking practices. Start at the first one. Press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear the model sentence. Listen two times. Then say it out loud yourself, in a big clear voice. I expect a whole sentence, like "I use water to drink." — not just one word. 2. Now record yourself. Press the microphone button. Say your sentence out loud, nice and slow. Then press the microphone again to stop. I expect you to wait one little second before you speak, so your first word is not cut off. 3. Next, listen to yourself. Press play and hear your own recording. Ask yourself: can I hear every word? I expect you to really listen, not skip this bit. This button also wakes up the Submit button. 4. Now press Submit for pronunciation check. It turns on after you have listened back. Read what the checker tells you, or ask your grown-up to read it. If you want to say it better, just record again. Do steps 1 to 4 for every one of the 6 practices. 5. Under the practices there is a slide deck called Use your voice. It has one practice on each slide. Press Start. Then press Hear model and listen. Say it yourself out loud. Press Record, say it, and then press Submit. Press the arrow to go to the next practice, and do the same again until the slides are done. 6. Last of all, scroll to the bottom and press the Finish speaking practices button. Press it only when you have spoken in every practice and every slide. You will know the page is finished when all 6 practices have your recording, the slides are all done, and you have pressed Finish speaking practices. Go and do step 1 now. Tell me when you have said your first sentence out loud, and tell me which sentence it was! 💧

activities.label: Activities
activities.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Activities page in Unit 8, Wonderful Water. On this page you will colour, draw, match, act, point and play with water. We do these to help you say water words out loud and use them in little sentences. By the end, you will be able to say things like "I use water to wash" and "The leaf floats." You need a pencil, some crayons, a bowl of water with a grown-up, and your speaking voice. Let's start! 1. Look at the top of the page. There are 6 activities. Read the words for each one. If reading is hard, press Hear the instructions and listen carefully. I expect you to listen right to the end before you begin. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Now do Activity 1. Colour the things that use water: the cup, the plant, the washing hands and the pot of soup. Say each one out loud as you colour it. Any colours you like are fine. I expect four things coloured and four names said. 3. Do Activity 2. Draw yourself using water. Then say the sentence: "I use water to ___." You can choose drink, wash, or water the plants. If there is a box, write your word in it. I expect one drawing and one full sentence said out loud. 4. Do Activity 3. Draw a line from each word to its place: rain goes to the sky, fish goes to the sea, tap goes to the kitchen, puddle goes to the road. Say each word as you draw the line. I expect four lines and four words spoken. 5. Do Activity 4. Stand up and act out the weather. Splash in the rain. Shiver in the wind. Shade your eyes in the sun. Say the weather word each time: rain, wind, sun. I expect three actions and three words. Be big and brave with your acting! 6. Do Activity 5. Point to the four water animals: fish, frog, duck and crab. For each one say, "A ___ lives in water." I expect all four found and four sentences said. 7. Do Activity 6. With your grown-up, put a leaf, a stone, a spoon and a cork in water. Guess first! Then look and sort them into two piles: floats and sinks. Say "The ___ floats" or "The ___ sinks." I expect an honest answer about what you really saw. 8. After each activity, press Mark complete. Only press it when you have really done that one. That button tells the page you finished it. 9. Now scroll down to the slides at the bottom. This part is called Learn by doing. There is one activity on each slide. 10. On the first slide, press Start. Do what the slide asks, out loud or on paper. Then press Mark complete. Then press the arrow to go to the next slide. Do the same on every slide. 11. On the last slide, press Finish activities. That finishes the slide deck. 12. Last of all, press Finish activities at the bottom of the page. Press it only when all six activities and all the slides are done. You will know the page is finished when every activity says complete and you have pressed Finish activities at the bottom. Brilliant work — now tell me, which activity was your favourite?

writing.label: Writing
writing.text: Hello! Today I am your writing teacher, and this is our Writing page for Wonderful Water. On this page you will draw, trace, copy and write little sentences about water. We do this because writing helps your water words stick in your head — words like rain, wet, dry, float and waste. By the end, you will have written your own sentence, all by yourself. You need a pencil, some paper for drawing, and your voice for saying words out loud. A grown-up can sit with you. Here is what I expect from you: say your idea out loud first, then write it. Use the model to help you. Neat letters, one capital letter at the start, and a full stop at the end. At least eight words in the big box. There are 5 steps. Here they all are. Step 1. Look at the list of 6 writing tasks. Choose one and press it. Read the task, and if you see a speaker, press Hear the task and listen carefully. Doing it well means listening right to the end before you start. I expect you to know what the task is asking before you pick up your pencil. Step 2. Press View model text. This shows you one good example, like "I use water to wash." Read it out loud, or ask your grown-up to read it with you. Look at the capital letter at the start and the full stop at the end. I expect you to copy the shape of the model, but use your own idea. Step 3. Now write your own in the big box. Write at least eight words — that is about two short sentences. Read the Writer's checklist and tick each thing you did. If you feel stuck, press Support for extra help. If it feels easy, press Challenge and do a little more. I expect a true idea about water, with your best letters. Step 4. Press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved, so you can come back and make it even better later. Then go back to the list and do the next task, one after another, until all 6 are done. I expect you to finish every task, not just your favourite one. Step 5. Now look at the slides at the bottom of the page, called Plan, write and improve. There is one task on each slide. Press Start, say your idea out loud, then write your sentences in the box — at least eight words again. Press Submit this draft, then press the arrow to go to the next task. I expect you to keep going slide by slide, taking your time. You will know the page is finished when all 6 writing tasks are submitted, and every slide in the deck has been started, written and submitted too. Ready? Start with Step 1 — choose your task and tell me which one you picked. 💧

games.label: Games
games.text: Hello! Today we are on the Games page for our unit, Wonderful Water. This is the fun part! You will play little games with our water words — words like rain, wet, dry, float and sink. Games help the words stick in your head, so later you can say them all by yourself. You need only your finger or mouse, your voice for saying words out loud, and a happy try-again heart. A grown-up nearby can read tricky words with you. Here is what to do, step by step. Step 1. Press a game to open it. Just tap one game box on the screen — any one you like. Then play it! When you get something right, you earn stars and XP. If a game feels hard, press the hint button and try again. Trying again is not cheating — it is learning. I expect you to say each word out loud as you play, even quietly, so your mouth learns the word too. Step 2. Play every game at least once. Go back and press the next game box, then the next, until you have opened them all. You may play a game more than once to get more stars — that is a great idea! I expect you to give every game a real try, even the one that looks hardest. Mistakes are how we learn. Step 3. When you have played them all, press the button that says I have played them all. That tells the page you are finished. If you get every game perfect, the page will finish all by itself — you will not need to press anything. I expect you to press it only when you truly played each game, because honest work is the best work. You will know the page is done when your stars are counted and the page moves you on, or the game boxes show you have finished them. Ready? Press your first game now, and tell me which one you chose. 🌊

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text: Hello! Today we finish our Wonderful Water unit with the checkpoint quiz. A quiz is a little check to see what you remember. We do it so you can feel proud of all the water words you learned. You will need your eyes, your thinking, and a grown-up sitting near you. I cannot tell you the answers — but I know you can do this! 1. First, look at question one on your screen. Read it slowly, or ask your grown-up to read it aloud. Then look at all four choices before you pick. Think: which one is about water? Tap the answer you think is right, then move to the next question. Do this for all ten questions, one at a time. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Here is how to think, not the answer. Some questions ask about a word, like wet or dry. Say the word out loud and picture it in your head. Wet is like your socks after a puddle. Dry is like a towel in the sun. The picture in your head helps you choose. 3. Some questions ask about float and sink. Float means it stays on top of the water, like a leaf. Sink means it goes down to the bottom, like a heavy stone. Put your hand flat on the table for float, then drop it low for sink. That little action helps you remember. 4. Some questions ask about a full sentence, like weather sentences. Read the whole sentence in your head. Ask yourself: does this sound right when I say it? We say "It is..." for the weather. Choose the one that sounds like real talking. 5. When you finish question ten, your score will show on the screen. You pass when you get more than half right — that means six or more out of ten. Look at your score together with your grown-up and smile. Every question you got right is something you truly learned! 6. If your score is not high enough, press Try again. Do the quiz once more, but this time go even slower. Think about the words we practised: rain, wet, dry, float, sink, plant, wash. Mistakes are how we learn. 7. When your score is good, press Continue. That takes you to My progress, where you can see all your work. Pressing Continue is what saves your finish — so don't forget it! You will know the page is finished when you have answered all ten questions, seen your score, and pressed Continue to reach My progress. Ready? Start with question one, and come tell me how it goes! 🌊

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text: Hello! Today we are on the Books page. This is our reading time for Unit 8, Wonderful Water. You will pick a book, read it or watch it, and listen to the sounds in the pictures. Reading helps our water words stick, words like rain, well, float and sink. You need your eyes, your voice, and a comfy seat. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. Let's start! Step 1. Look at the shelf of books on your screen. Take your time and look at the covers. Choose one book and tap it to open it. If you see our story The Well in the Village, that one goes with our unit. I expect you to pick one book, not five, and to say the title out loud before you open it. Step 2. Now read the book page by page. Press the arrow to go forward to the next page. Press the other arrow if you want to go back and look again. If your book plays like a video, just watch and listen carefully. I expect you to read or listen to the words out loud, not silently, and to look at each picture before you turn the page. Step 3. Tap the pictures on each page to hear their sounds. Tap the rain, tap the water, tap the animals. Listen, then say the word back yourself. Say it with me, slowly: rain. I expect you to try saying each word after you hear it, even if it feels tricky. Step 4. Keep going right to the very end of the book. Do not stop in the middle. On the last page, press Finish book. That tells the page you are done. I expect you to reach the last page all by yourself, one arrow at a time. Step 5. One book finishes this page. If you loved it, go back to the shelf and read another one! More reading means more water words in your head. How will you know the page is finished? When you press Finish book on the last page, the page is complete. Then come and tell me one thing from your book, and one new word you heard. Take your time — there's no rush. 🌧️

overview.label: Overview
overview.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 9: City Places. This page is called the Overview. It is like standing at the door and peeking inside the room before you go in. We do it so you know what is coming, and then the whole unit feels easy. You need your eyes, your ears, and your voice. Let's start! 1. Read the unit preview on this page. It tells you what you will learn: places in a town like the shop, the market, the school, the hospital and the library. If you see a Listen button, press it and follow the words with your finger as they are read. I expect you to hear one place word you already know, and say it out loud. Good listening means sitting still and following along. 2. Read the four steps under How to learn. These four steps show how you will work on every page of this unit. Read them slowly, one at a time. A grown-up can read them to you if one is near. I expect you to know one thing you will do in this unit, like listen to a story or say a sentence. 3. Now press the button that says I have previewed this unit. This tells the page, "Yes, I looked and I am ready!" Only press it after you have read the preview and the four steps. I expect you to be honest and press it when you really have looked. 4. Last, press Open vocabulary. This takes you to the first learning page, where we meet the new words. I expect you to go there ready to talk, because we will say lots of words out loud together. You will know this page is finished when you have pressed I have previewed this unit and then Open vocabulary, and the new page opens. Take your time — there's no rush. Tell me when you have done step one, and I will be right here! 🌟

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Vocabulary page of Unit 9, City Places. On this page you will learn 52 words about our town — words like shop, market, library, doctor, near and next to. We learn them so you can talk about your own town in English. By the end, you will be able to say each word, tell what it means, and use it in a sentence. You need your voice, your eyes and your fingers to type. Take your time — there's no rush. Here are all the steps, one by one. 1. Look at the word list on the left side. Press one word. A card will open with that word on it. Start with the first word. You will do every word, one at a time. I expect you to press only one word and look at its card before you do anything else. 2. Press Hear it. Listen carefully. Now say the word out loud yourself. Then press Again and say it one more time, out loud — not in your head. I expect to hear your voice twice. Say it with me, slowly. 3. Now read the meaning on the card. Press the little speaker next to the meaning to hear it read to you. Then say what the word means in your own words. It does not have to match exactly. I expect a short try, like "a shop is where we buy things". 4. Look at In a sentence. Read a sentence, then press Hear sentence to listen to it. Use the arrows to go through every sentence on the card. Then pick one sentence and read it out loud yourself. I expect you to hear them all and read one with your own voice. 5. Look at the Spelling line on the card. Say each letter one by one, slowly, like s - h - o - p. Then say the whole word again. I expect careful letters, not fast ones. 6. Find the box that says Write your own sentence. Type a sentence with the word in it. The grey words help you start. Then press Check sentence. Read what the checker tells you and fix anything it points out. I expect one sentence that makes sense, with a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end. 7. When you can say the word, know its meaning, and have written your sentence, press I know this word. Now that word gets a LEARNED tag in the list. I expect you to press it only when all three parts are done — that is being honest with yourself. 8. Now press the next word in the list. Do steps 2 to 7 again for that word. Then the next, and the next. Little bits are best — a few words, then a rest, then a few more. 9. Under the word list there is a deck of slides with the same words, one word on each slide. If you like slides better, press Start on the first slide, the one that says Say the words. On each slide press Hear it and Again, then Meaning, then read the sentences and press Hear sentence, then look at the Spelling line, then open Write your own sentence, type your sentence and press Check sentence, then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right to move to the next slide — the little dots show where you are. On the last slide, when every word is marked, press the finish button. Cards at the top or slides at the bottom — both teach the same words, so choose the one you like. You will know the page is finished when every single word in the list has a LEARNED tag next to it, and no word is left plain. Off you go with your first word. When you have done step 2 for it, come and tell me, and I will listen. 🌟

lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text: Hello! Today we start Unit 9: City Places. This page is our video lesson. You will watch a teacher, hear the new words, and say them out loud with her. By the end you will know some town words like shop, market, school, hospital and library. You need your ears, your eyes and your voice. A grown-up can sit with you if one is nearby. Here is what I expect from you: sit up, look at the screen, and be brave with your voice. Let's go, step by step. 1. Press play on the video. That is the big arrow button in the middle. Watch it all the way to the end, without stopping. Look at the words at the bottom of the screen too — those are the captions. I expect you to keep watching to the very end, even if some words feel new. That is okay! New words become friends when we hear them. 2. Say the words out loud with the teacher in the video. When she says "market", you say "market" too. When she says a whole sentence, like "I go to the school", you say it with her. Say it with me, slowly. I expect a real voice, not a tiny whisper — big and clear, like you are talking to a friend across the room. Try to copy the way her mouth moves. 3. When the video has finished, press the button under it to go on to Vocabulary. Only press it after the video is all done. I expect you to finish watching first, then press. That button takes you to the next part of our lesson. You will know this page is finished when the video has ended, you have said the words out loud, and you have pressed the button to go to Vocabulary. Then come back and tell me one place word you heard. I would love to know! 🌟

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text: Hello! Today I am your reading teacher. This page is our reading shelf for Unit 9, City Places. On this shelf there are three texts. One is our story, "A Walk Around Town". One is our talk lines, "Talk about City Places". One is our rhyme with the traffic lights and the town song. We read them so we learn the town words like shop, market, library and hospital, and so we learn what red and green mean. You need your eyes, your finger, your voice, and a quiet spot. Here is what I expect from you: read slowly, point with your finger, and say the words out loud. It is fine to go slowly. Take your time — there's no rush. Here are your six steps. 1. Read the text that is on your screen. Look at the first word. Put your finger under it. Read it out loud, slowly, one word at a time. If a word is hard, sound it out or ask your grown-up. I expect your finger to move under every word, not skip along the line. 2. Now listen to it. Press Prepare audio, and wait a moment. Then press the play button. Follow the words with your finger while the voice reads. I expect your finger to stay with the voice. If you get lost, press play again and start over. That is good practice, not a mistake. 3. Some texts are for listening first. If your text is a listening text, listen all the way through first, then read along with it the second time. Read our story, "A Walk Around Town", very carefully. That story is the one our Comprehension questions are about, so notice the places Amal visits and the kind people she meets. 4. Now move along the shelf. Press Next text to go to the next one. Press Previous text if you want to go back and read one again. I expect you to read all three texts, not just one. Do the same each time: read it, then listen and follow with your finger. 5. Now look at the bottom of the page. There is a deck of slides with the same text, one small page at a time. On the first slide, press Start, which says "Read the story". On each page, read the words out loud, or press the speaker to hear them. Then press the arrow to turn the page. Keep going to the very last page. On the last page, press I have read this text. I expect you to read every slide page, not jump to the end. 6. When you have read all three texts and finished the slides, press Finished reading. You will know the page is done when you have pressed I have read this text on the last slide, and pressed Finished reading. Then your work is saved and this page is complete. Off you go and start with step one. Come back and tell me when your first text is read, and tell me one place you saw in it. 🌟

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Hello! Today we are doing Comprehension. That means: we read, then we think, then we answer. The questions are about our story "A Walk Around Town" and our talk lines. Doing this helps you remember the story and say your ideas in full sentences. You need your eyes for reading, your voice for saying, and your fingers for typing. A grown-up can sit with you and read the questions out loud. Ready? Here are all the steps. 1. There are 12 questions about the texts you read. Read the first question slowly. Then think about the story in your head. Ask yourself: what happened? who was there? I expect you to read the question twice before you answer. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Now type your answer in the box. Please write a full sentence, not just one word. So not "hospital", but "The doctor works at the hospital." Say your sentence out loud first, then type it. Start with a big capital letter and end with a full stop. 3. When your sentence is in the box, press Check guidance. This shows you a good answer. Read it and compare: is your idea the same? Your words do not have to match exactly — your own words are lovely. If your box is empty, the page will ask you to write first, so always type before you press. Do this for every one of the 12 questions. 4. Now look at the bottom of the page. There is a deck of slides called Think about the story, with one question on each slide. Press Start. Read the question, then say your answer out loud in a big, clear voice. Then press Check guidance to see a good answer. Press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going, one slide at a time. 5. On the last slide, press Finish comprehension. Then press Finish comprehension at the bottom of the page too, when all 12 questions and all the slides are done. You will know the page is finished when every question has your sentence in its box, every slide has been said out loud, and you have pressed Finish comprehension. Then come and tell me one thing you remembered about Amal's town. Great work today!

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Grammar page in our unit, City Places. Grammar means the way we put words together to make a good sentence. On this page you will learn six little sentence patterns about our town, like "There is a shop" and "I go to the market." We do this so you can talk about your town in English and people understand you. By the end you will be able to say all six patterns out loud by yourself. All you need is your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby if you have one. Here is our whole plan. There are five steps. Step 1: Read and listen to each lesson. There are 6 grammar lessons on the page. Start at the first one. Read the rule and look at the examples. Then press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear it read to you. Listen carefully, like a detective. I expect you to press the speaker at least once for every lesson, and to listen right to the end before you move on. Step 2: Say the examples out loud. After you listen, say each example yourself in a big, clear voice. Say it with me, slowly. For example: "There is a shop." "The shop is next to the school." Do not just read it in your head — your mouth needs the practice too! I expect a real out-loud voice, and it is fine to say it two or three times until it feels easy. Step 3: Do the practice in every lesson. Under each lesson, press Show practice. Try the practice sentences out loud, putting your own town words in the gaps. Then press Hear the practice to check how they sound. Did yours sound the same? Well done if it did! Do this for all 6 lessons, one at a time, no skipping. I expect you to try first, then listen — trying first is what makes your brain strong. Step 4: Do the slides at the bottom. Under the lessons there is a slide deck called Say the patterns. Press Start. On each slide there is one pattern. Say the pattern out loud, then try the practice on that slide, then press the speaker to hear it. Move on to the next slide and do the same. Keep going all the way to the last slide. I expect you to speak on every slide, even the tricky ones. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 5: Press the button. When you have done all 6 lessons and all the slides, press the I practised all the lessons button at the bottom of the page. Only press it when you really have done them all — that button is your honest tick. You will know the page is finished when you have listened to all 6 lessons, said the examples out loud, done every practice, reached the last slide, and pressed I practised all the lessons. Now start with Step 1, lesson one. When you have listened to it, come back and tell me, and I will help you with the next bit. 🌟

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text: Hello! Today I am your speaking teacher, and this page is all about your voice. On this page you will practise six short town sentences out loud. You will hear them, say them, record them, and listen to yourself. We do this so your mouth gets used to English words like shop, market, library and hospital. By the end, you will be able to say "There is a shop" and "I go to the market" all by yourself, nice and clear. What you need: your voice, your ears, and a grown-up nearby to help you press the buttons. What I expect from you: say the words out loud, not in your head. Speak slowly and clearly, like you are telling a friend something important. It is fine to try again. Mistakes are how we learn. Here are all the steps. 1. Listen and say. There are 6 speaking practices on the page. For each one, press the speaker button, or press Replay, to hear the model sentence. Listen two times. Watch how the voice says each word. Then say the same sentence out loud yourself. I expect a full sentence, like "There is a shop", not just one word. 2. Record. Press the microphone button. Then say your sentence in a clear voice. When you finish, press the microphone again to stop. Take a little breath first, and try not to rush. I expect your whole sentence in one go, from the first word to the last. 3. Listen back. Play your recording and listen to yourself. Ask yourself: can I hear every word? Was I loud enough? This is my favourite part, because you get to be your own teacher for a moment. 4. Submit. Press Submit for pronunciation check. This button turns on only after you have listened back, so do step 3 first. Read what the checker says about your words. If you want to say it better, record again and submit again. Do steps 1, 2, 3 and 4 for every one of the 6 practices. 5. The slides at the bottom. Under the practices there is a slide deck called Use your voice, with one practice on each slide. Press Start. Then press Hear model and listen. Say it yourself out loud. Press Record, say your sentence, and then press Submit. Press the arrow to go to the next practice, and do the same thing again until the slides are done. 6. Finish. When you have done all the practices and all the slides, press the Finish speaking practices button at the bottom of the page. You will know the page is finished when every practice has a recording you have submitted, the slides have no more arrows to press, and you have pressed Finish speaking practices. Only your press counts, so do not forget that last button! Ready? Start with practice one and press the speaker. Tell me when you have said your first sentence out loud, and I will be right here. 🌟

writing.label: Writing
writing.text: Hello! Today I am your writing teacher, and this is our Writing page for Unit 9, City Places. Writing means putting our town words on paper. We will write about places like the shop, the market, the library and the hospital. We do this so you can say AND show what you know. By the end, you will have your own little writing about your town. You need a pencil, some paper for drawing, and your reading eyes. A grown-up can sit with you and read the words out loud. Here is our whole plan, step by step. Step 1. Look at the list of writing tasks. There are 6 of them. Click the first one to open it. Read the task, and if you see a little speaker, press Hear the task and listen carefully. I expect you to listen right to the end, then say out loud what you must do. Our six tasks are: draw and tell, trace two words, match and copy, add labels, finish "I go to the ___", and write a polite sentence. Step 2. Press View model text. This shows you an example of good writing, like mine. Read it with your grown-up. Do not copy it word for word. Just look at how it starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. I expect you to notice one thing you can use in your own writing. Step 3. Now write your own in the big box. Say your sentence out loud first, then write it. Try for eight words or more, like "There is a market next to my school." Use the sentence starter from the task, such as "There is a", "A", "I go to the", or "Please". Then open the Writer's checklist and check each thing: capital letter at the start, finger spaces, and a full stop at the end. If you feel stuck, press Support for help. If it feels easy, press Challenge and do a bit more. I expect a real place from your own town, not just any word. Step 4. Press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved, so nothing gets lost. You can come back and make it better any time. Now do the next task the same way, until all 6 tasks are done. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 5. Scroll down to the slides at the bottom. This deck is called Plan, write and improve, and it has one task on each slide. Press Start. Write your sentences in the box, again eight words or more, then press Submit this draft. Then press the arrow to go to the next task. Keep going until the last slide. You will know the page is finished when all 6 writing tasks are submitted and all the slides in the deck are submitted too. Then read your best sentence out loud to a grown-up, or to yourself in a big proud voice. Ready? Start with Step 1 and tell me which task you picked. 🙂

activities.label: Activities
activities.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Activities page in Unit 9, City Places. These activities let you play with our town words: shop, market, school, hospital, library, park. You will colour, draw, act and talk. We do this so the words stay in your head and come out of your mouth easily. Get your crayons, some paper, and your brave speaking voice ready. Here is what I expect from you: try every activity, say the words out loud, and do your best drawing. Neat is nice, but talking is the most important part. Here are your steps. Step 1. Look at the top of the page. There are 6 activities. Read the instructions for the first one, and press Hear the instructions to listen to them. Listen carefully, all the way to the end. If you did not catch it, press Hear the instructions again. That is fine — good learners listen twice. Step 2. Now do the activity. Some activities ask you to write your answer in the box. Say your answer out loud first, then write it in the box. Write the words you know, and do not worry about spelling — just try. For the drawing ones, use colours and make each place look like a real place in a town. Step 3. When you have finished one activity, press Mark complete under that activity. Only press it after you really did the work. Then go to the next activity and do Steps 1, 2 and 3 again, until all 6 are marked complete. Step 4. Now scroll down to the bottom of the page. There is a deck of slides called Learn by doing, with one activity on each slide. Press Start. Do the activity on the slide, then press Mark complete. Then press the arrow to go to the next slide. Keep going, slide by slide. On the last slide, press Finish activities. Step 5. Last of all, press Finish activities at the bottom of the page. Press it only when all 6 activities and all the slides are done. You will know the page is finished when every activity shows Mark complete pressed, and you have pressed Finish activities at the bottom. Now start with Step 1 — press Hear the instructions for Activity 1, and tell me what it asks you to do. Take your time — there's no rush.

games.label: Games
games.text:
Hello! Today we are on the Games page for our unit, City Places. 🎮

These games help you practise our town words — shop, market, school, hospital, library and park. They also help you remember that red means stop and green means go. Playing is a real way to learn, because your brain remembers words best when you are having fun. By the end, you will know these words much better. What I expect from you: try your best, say each word out loud as you play, and use a hint if you get stuck. Getting one wrong is fine — mistakes are how we learn. Here are the three steps. Step 1. Press one game to open it. Any game is a good one to start with. Then play it. When a town word comes up, say it out loud with your mouth, not just in your head. You will earn stars and XP for what you know. If a question feels hard, press the hint button, or try again — hints and retries are always there for you. I expect you to finish that one game all the way to the end. Step 2. Now play every game on the page at least once. Open one, play it, then come back and open the next one. Do not skip a game because it looks tricky — that is the one that will teach you the most! When you have played them all, you may go back and play again to win more stars. I expect every game to have been played by you at least one time. Step 3. When you have played them all, press the button that says I have played them all. Only press it when it is really true. If you master every single game, you do not need to press it — the page will finish all by itself. You will know the page is finished when it tells you so, either after you press I have played them all, or on its own when every game is mastered. Ready? Press your first game now, and come back and tell me which one you chose. 🌟

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text: Hello! Today is our City Places checkpoint. That means a little quiz. It shows you how many town words you already know. You do not need a pencil — just your eyes, your thinking, and a grown-up nearby if you like. I expect you to try every question, even the tricky ones. Here are our steps. 1. First, the questions. There are 10 of them. Read each question slowly, twice. Then look at all the answer choices before you pick. Ask yourself: "Which one is a PLACE in a town?" or "Who works there?" or "What does that colour mean?" Then click the one answer you think is right. I expect one answer for every question, chosen by you. I cannot tell you the answers — but I can give you a hint any time. Just ask me! 2. Next, your score. When you finish all 10, the page shows how many you got right. More than half right means you passed. Take a breath and look at your score. I expect you to be proud of it, because you tried your best. Mistakes are how we learn. 3. Last, what to do with your score. If your score is not high enough, press Try again and do the quiz one more time. Go a bit slower this time, and think about the ones that were tricky. When your score is good, press Continue. That takes you to My progress. You will know the page is finished when you have answered all 10 questions, seen your score, and pressed Continue to go to My progress. Ready for question one? Go ahead and start, and tell me if you want a hint. Take your time — there's no rush. 🌟

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text: Hello! Today we are on the Books page. This is our reading time. You will pick a book about our town and read it all the way through. Books help you meet our unit words again, like shop, market, hospital, library and next to. All you need are your eyes, your ears, your finger for tapping, and your reading voice. Let's start! 1. Choose a book from the shelf. Look at the shelf on your screen. Look at each cover picture and the title. Pick one that looks fun to you. Then tap that book to open it. I expect you to choose by yourself — every book on the shelf is a good choice. 2. Read it page by page with the arrows. Press the arrow to turn to the next page, and the back arrow if you want to see a page again. Read slowly, out loud if you can. If your book plays as a video, just watch and listen carefully. I expect you to say the words with the book, not rush the pages. 3. Tap the pictures to hear their sounds. On each page, tap a picture, like a shop or a bus. Listen to the word, then say it back in your own voice. Say it with me, slowly. I expect you to tap at least two or three pictures on the pages you read. 4. Read or watch it right to the end. Keep pressing the arrow until you reach the last page. Do not stop in the middle — the best part is often at the end! I expect you to look at every page, even the ones with lots of words. 5. Press Finish book on the last page. When you get to the last page, find the button that says Finish book and press it. That is how the page knows you have read your book. I expect you to press it yourself, at the end, not before. 6. Read more if you like. One book finishes this page, but you may go back to the shelf and choose another one. More reading means more town words in your head. That is always a happy extra. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed Finish book on the last page of one book. Then come and tell me one place from your book, and one word you liked. Take your time — there's no rush. 📚

overview.label: Overview
overview.text:
Hello! Today we start Unit 10: My First English World. This page is called the Overview. It is like looking at a map before a trip. It tells you what you will learn and how you will learn it. You only need your eyes, your ears, and your reading voice. Let's look at that together. 1. Read the unit preview on this page. Look for the Listen button and press it if you can see one. Then follow the words with your finger while you listen. Read slowly. I expect you to find one thing you will make in this unit — it is a little book with six pages. Say it out loud to yourself: "I will make a six-page book."

2. Now read the four steps under How to learn. These four steps tell you how every page of this unit will work. Read them one at a time, from the top. If a word is hard, say it slowly, sound by sound, or ask your grown-up. I expect you to know one thing after this: what you do first on each page. 3. Last, press the button that says I have previewed this unit. That button tells the page you are ready. Then press Open vocabulary. That takes you to the first learning page, where we meet our words. Press gently and wait for the new page to open. You will know this page is finished when the Overview has its tick and the vocabulary page is open on your screen. That means you are ready to begin your capstone. Take your time — there's no rush. Tell me when you have pressed I have previewed this unit! 🌟

dictionary.label: Vocabulary
dictionary.text: Hello! Today we are learning our words for this unit. There are 64 words, and many of them are old friends from this year. Words are the bricks we build sentences with, so the more you know, the more you can say. By the end of this page you will be able to say each word, tell what it means, and write your own sentence with it. You need your voice, your eyes, and your fingers for typing. Here are the steps. There are 9. 1. Look at the word list on the left side. Press one word. A card opens for that word. Start with the first word, and we will do them one at a time. I expect you to work slowly, one word only, not jumping around. 2. On the card, press Hear it. Listen carefully. Now say the word out loud yourself. Then press Again and say it one more time. Say it with your real voice, not in your head — your mouth needs the practice too. 3. Now read the meaning on the card. Press the little speaker next to it to hear the meaning read to you. Then say the meaning in your own words. It does not need to match exactly. I just want to hear that you understand it. 4. Next, look at In a sentence. Read the sentence. Press Hear sentence to listen to it. Use the arrows to see every sentence for that word. Then pick one sentence and read it out loud yourself, nice and clear. 5. Now look at the Spelling on the card. Say the letters one by one, slowly. Then say the whole word again. This helps your eyes and your ears remember the word together. 6. Now it is your turn to write. Find Write your own sentence and type a sentence with the word in the box. The grey words help you start. Press Check sentence. Read what the checker tells you, and fix anything it points out. I expect a short sentence that makes sense — a good one is enough, it does not need to be long. 7. When you can say the word, tell its meaning, and you have written your sentence, press I know this word. Now that word gets a LEARNED tag in the list. Only press it when all three parts are really done. 8. Now press the next word in the list. Do the very same steps again with that word. Take your time — there is no rush. A few words each day is very good work. 9. There is another way too, if you like it better. Under the word list there is a deck of slides, one word on each slide. Press Start on the first slide, which says Say the words. On each slide, press Hear it and Again and say the word, press Meaning to hear what it means, read the sentences and press Hear sentence, look at the Spelling line, then open Write your own sentence, type your sentence and press Check sentence. Then press I know this word. Press the arrow on the right to go to the next slide. The dots under the slide show where you are. On the last slide, when every word is marked, press the finish button. The cards at the top and the slides at the bottom teach the same words, so choose the one you like. You will know the page is finished when every word in the list has a LEARNED tag, or you have pressed the finish button on the last slide. Now press your first word and start with step 2. Tell me when you have said it out loud, and I will be right here. 🌟
