lecture.label: Video lesson
lecture.text: Hello! Today we start our very last unit: My First English World. This page is the lesson launch. It tells you about your big capstone project — your own six-page picture-and-word book. By the end of this page, you will know what you are going to make. You just need your eyes, your ears, your voice, and a comfy chair. One small note first: this unit is a project unit, so the launch may be a short story instead of a moving video. If nothing plays, that is okay! You can read the story "Amal's English Year" on the Reading page instead. There are three steps on this page. Step 1. Press the play button on the video lesson. Watch it all the way to the end. Sit still and listen carefully. Look at the words on the screen too — those are the captions. Try to follow them with your eyes. I expect you to watch the whole thing, not stop in the middle. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 2. Now use your voice. When the teacher in the video says a word or a sentence, say it out loud too. Say it at the same time, or right after. Say it clearly, not in a tiny whisper. I expect to hear you say sentences like "My name is ___." and "I can ___." Your mouth learns English by saying it, not just by hearing it. Step 3. When the video has finished, look under it. Press the button there to go on to Vocabulary. That is where we will meet our review words. I expect you to press it yourself, so the page knows you are done. You will know this page is finished when the video has played all the way to the end, you have said the words out loud, and you have pressed the button to go to Vocabulary. Ready? Press play now, and tell me when the video is done. 🙂

reading.label: Reading & story
reading.text: Hello! Today we are on the Reading and story page. This is where we read the three texts of our capstone unit. Reading them helps you learn the words, hear how sentences sound, and get ready for the questions later. You need your eyes, your finger, your voice, and a quiet spot. Let's start! 1. Look at the reading shelf. There are 3 texts there. Read the text on the screen slowly. Point at each word with your finger as you go. Read it out loud if you can — even in a small voice. I expect you to read every word, not just look at the picture. 2. Now press Prepare audio. Wait a moment. Then press the play button. Listen carefully and follow the words with your finger. Try to keep your finger on the same word the voice is saying. That is how good readers do it. 3. If a text is a listening text, listen first, then read along. One of these texts is our story, "Amal's English Year". That is the one the Comprehension questions will ask about. So read that one extra carefully and try to remember what Amal did. 4. Press Next text to go to the second text, and Next text again for the third. If you want to go back, press Previous text. I expect you to read all three, not just one. Take your time — there's no rush. 5. Now look at the bottom of the page. There is a deck of slides with the same text, one small page at a time. Press Start on the first slide, "Read the story". On each page, read the words, or press the speaker to hear them. Then press the arrow to turn the page. On the last page, press I have read this text. 6. When you have read all three texts, press Finished reading. You will know the page is done when you have pressed I have read this text on the slides and Finished reading at the top. Then the page has its tick, and you are ready for the questions. Start with step 1 now, and tell me when you have read the first text. Ready?

grammar.label: Grammar
grammar.text: Hello! Today I am your teacher for the Grammar page. Let's look at that together. On this page you will learn six speaking patterns. They are: My name is ___, I can ___, I like ___, This is a / an ___, It is ___, and My next goal is ___. These are the sentences you will use in your capstone book and in your one-minute talk. So this page gets your mouth ready for celebration day! What I expect from you: sit up tall, use your speaking voice, and say every sentence out loud. Not whispering. Not just reading in your head. Out loud, like you are telling a friend. Have a grown-up nearby if you can. Here are your steps. 1. Look at the first lesson at the top of the page. Read the title and the rule. Then press the speaker button, or press Replay, and listen carefully. Listen with your eyes on the words. I expect you to hear the whole thing before you speak. If you want to hear it twice, press Replay again. That is a smart thing to do. 2. Now say the examples out loud. Say them slowly and clearly. Take a breath first, then speak. For lesson one you will say things like My name is Maya. Say your OWN name too. A good try sounds clear enough for someone across the room to hear you. 3. Under that lesson, press Show practice. Try each practice sentence with your own words. Then press Hear the practice and listen. Ask yourself, did I sound like that? If not, say it one more time. I expect you to try every practice sentence, not just the first one. 4. Now do steps 1, 2 and 3 again for every lesson, all six of them. Lesson two is I can ___. Try to say a DIFFERENT skill each time, like I can read words, I can count to twenty, I can spell my name. Lesson three is I like ___. Careful here: we say I like books, not I am like books. Put your hands on your heart when you say I like. 5. Lesson four is This is a / an ___. Here is the tricky bit. We say a cup and a chair, but an apple and an umbrella. If the word starts with an open-mouth sound, a, e, i, o, u, we say an. Look around your room and name three real things you can see. 6. Lesson five is It is ___. This one describes. Name the thing first, then say what it is like: It is blue. It is small. Do not name the thing twice. Ask yourself, what is it like? Lesson six is My next goal is ___. A goal is something new, something you cannot do yet. Point your finger forward when you say it. 7. Now go to the bottom of the page. There is a slide deck called Say the patterns. Press Start. On each slide, say the pattern out loud, try the practice, then press the speaker to hear it. Keep going, slide after slide, until you reach the last slide. Do not skip any. I expect your voice on every single slide. 8. Last step! When you have done all six lessons and all the slides, press the button at the bottom that says I practised all the lessons. You will know the page is finished when you have pressed I practised all the lessons and the page shows it is done. Only press it if you really said everything out loud — that button is your honest word. Take your time — there's no rush. Come back and tell me when you finish a lesson, and I will listen to your sentences. Which lesson are you starting with?

comprehension.label: Comprehension
comprehension.text: Hello! Today we are doing Comprehension. That word means: I read or listen, and then I show I understood. We are doing it because you listened to three texts about Amal and her English year. Answering questions helps the story stick in your head, and it helps you speak and write in full sentences. You need your eyes, your thinking brain, and your fingers for typing. A grown-up can sit nearby and help you type. Here is what I expect from you: think first, then answer in a full sentence, and try before you look at the guidance. Your answer does not need to be perfect. Trying is the important part. 1. Look at the first question. There are 12 questions in all. Read it slowly, or ask your grown-up to read it to you. Then think about the story "Amal's English Year", the project brief "My Capstone Steps", or the "Celebration Dialogue". If you forget, scroll up and read that bit again. That is allowed! I expect you to think before you type. 2. Now type your answer in the box. Try to write a full sentence, not just one word. So instead of "folder", write "Amal found her work in her folder." Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Say it out loud first, then write it — that makes it easier. 3. Press Check guidance. This shows you a good answer. Compare it with yours: did you say the same idea? Your words can be different — that is fine! If your box is empty, the page will ask you to write something first, so always type before you press. Do this for every one of the 12 questions. 4. Now go down to the slides at the bottom. This part is called "Think about the story". There is one question on each slide. Press Start. Say your answer out loud in a big, clear voice. Then press Check guidance to see a good answer. Then press the arrow to go to the next question. Keep going, one slide at a time. On the very last slide, press Finish comprehension. 5. Last of all, press Finish comprehension at the bottom of the page. Only press it when every question has an answer and every slide is done. You will know the page is finished when all 12 boxes have your writing in them, the slides are all done, and you have pressed Finish comprehension. Then the page is complete and you can be proud. Ready? Start with question one, and tell me when you have typed your answer. Take your time — there's no rush.

writing.label: Writing
writing.text:
Hello! Today I am your writing teacher. This page is where you make your own book, My First English World. There are six little pages. On each one you draw a picture and write one short sentence. We do this because it shows everything you learned in Grade 1. At the end, you will have a whole book you made yourself! You will need a pencil, paper or a screen for drawing, and your thinking brain. I expect you to try every task, write at least eight words, and read your sentence out loud. Neat is nice, but brave is better. Mistakes are how we learn. Here are the steps. 1. Look at the list of six writing tasks. Press the first one to open it. Read the task slowly. If you see a speaker, press Hear the task and listen. I expect you to know two things after this: what to draw, and what sentence to start with. For page 1 the start is "My name is ". 2. Press View model text. This shows you a good example, like "My name is Amina." Do not copy it word for word. Look at how it starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. I expect you to say, "Ah, now I see how mine should look."

3. Now write your own in the big box. Say your sentence out loud first, then write it. Use at least eight words in the box — that means your sentence plus one or two labels or an extra line. Use the Writer's checklist to check your work. If you feel stuck, press Support. If it feels easy, press Challenge and add one more sentence. I expect a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end. 4. Press Submit this draft. Your writing is saved, so it is safe. You can come back later and make it better. Then do the next task, and the next, until all six are done. I expect you to finish all six tasks: My name is, I can, I like, This is a, It is, and My next goal is. 5. Now go to the slides at the bottom of the page. This deck is called Plan, write and improve, and it has one task on each slide. Press Start. Write your sentences in the box — again, at least eight words. Press Submit this draft. Then press the arrow to go to the next task. Keep going until you have done every slide. You will know the page is finished when every writing task has been submitted and every slide has been submitted too. Then your six book pages are done. Ready? Start with task one, and tell me when you have read it. Take your time — there's no rush.

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.text: Hello! Today is our Speaking page, and this is a happy one. You are going to practise your capstone talk out loud. That is the little show-and-tell about your book, My First English World. Speaking your words makes them stick in your mouth and your memory. You need your voice, your ears, and a nice big smile. Let's begin! 1. Look at the first speaking practice. Press the speaker button, or press Replay, and listen to the model. Listen twice — once to hear the words, once to hear the music of the voice. Then say it out loud yourself. I expect a real voice, not a whisper. Stand tall, take a breath, and say it slowly and clearly, like this: "Assalamu alaikum. My name is..." with your own name. 2. Now record yourself. Press the microphone button, say your sentence, then press the microphone again to stop. Say your whole sentence in one go. It is fine to start again if you giggle — lots of children do! 3. Next, listen to yourself. Press play and hear your own recording. Ask yourself two things: could I hear every word, and did I speak slowly enough? This is the part where you are your own teacher. 4. Then press Submit for pronunciation check. That button wakes up after you have listened back. Read what the checker tells you, or ask your grown-up to read it with you. If it says a word was hard to hear, record that sentence again and try that word bigger and slower. I expect you to do these same four things — hear the model, say it, record, listen, submit — for all six practices, not just the first one. Take your time; there is no rush. 5. Under the practices there is a slide deck called Use your voice, with one practice on each slide. Press Start. On each slide, press Hear model, then say it yourself out loud, then press Record, then press Submit. When that slide is done, press the arrow to go to the next practice. Keep going until you have said every slide. 6. Last of all, press the Finish speaking practices button at the bottom of the page. Only press it when all six practices and all the slides are done. You will know the page is finished when every practice has your voice recorded, you have pressed Submit on each one, and the Finish speaking practices button is pressed. Then your talk is ready to share with your family. Take your time — there's no rush. Come and tell me when you finish practice one, and I will listen to how it went!

activities.label: Activities
activities.text:
Hello! Today you are the maker. This Activities page is where you build your capstone — your big Grade 1 project. You will hunt for your best work, sort words, retell a story, make your little book, practise your talk, and share it. We do this so everything you learned this year comes together in one book you can hold. Get a pencil, your crayons, your learning folder, and your happy voice ready. Here is your guide. Six activities, five steps. Take your time — there's no rush. 1. Read each activity first. There are 6 activities on the page. For each one, read the instructions. Then press Hear the instructions and listen. Listening helps your ears learn the words too. I expect you to know what to do BEFORE you start. If you are not sure, read it one more time. 2. Now do the activity. Activity 1 is Portfolio treasure hunt — look in your folder for your neatest writing, a coloured picture, a word list, and one hard piece. Activity 2 is Thirty-word picture sort — put your word cards in piles: school, family, animals, town. Read each pile out loud. Activity 3 is Story retell — put four pictures in order and tell the story with First, Then, Next, Last. Activity 4 is Mini-book making — fold three sheets, ask a grown-up to staple the middle, add your six pages, and draw a cover with your name. Activity 5 is One-minute rehearsal — stand tall, hold your book out, and talk for one minute. Activity 6 is Celebration showcase — say hello, read two pages, say your next goal, and thank your family. Some activities have a box. Write your answer in the box. Say it out loud first, then write it. I expect real words, not just marks — a label or a short sentence like "I like the farm."

3. Press Mark complete. When one activity is finished, press Mark complete under that activity. Only press it after you really did the work. That button tells the page, "I did this one!"

4. Then go to the slides at the bottom. Under the activities there is a deck called Learn by doing, with one activity on each slide. Press Start. Do that activity. Press Mark complete. Then press the arrow to go to the next slide. Do the same on every slide. On the last slide, press Finish activities. 5. Last of all, press Finish activities at the bottom of the page. Press it only when all six activities have a tick and all the slides are done. You will know the page is finished when every activity shows Mark complete pressed, and you have pressed Finish activities at the bottom. Then your capstone work is saved. 🎉

Shall we start with Activity 1, the treasure hunt? Go and get your folder, then tell me what you find.

quiz.label: Quiz
quiz.text: Well done for getting all the way here! This is your checkpoint quiz for Unit 10. It shows what you remember from your whole first year of English — words, sentences, animals, senses and town places. You need your eyes, your thinking, and a calm, slow head. I will not tell you any answers, but I will show you how to think. Here are all the steps. 1. There are 10 questions. Press the answer you choose for each one. Read the question twice before you answer. Then read all four choices, right to the end — do not stop at the first one that looks nice. Ask yourself, "What is this question really asking?" If it asks for a colour, look for a colour. If it asks for a farm animal, look for an animal. If it asks which one is a whole sentence, look for a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end. I expect you to try every question, even a tricky one. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. If one question feels hard, say the sentence out loud with each choice in it. Your ears often know the right one before your eyes do. For example, with "This is ___ apple," say it both ways and listen for which one sounds smooth. Guessing your best guess is fine — never leave a question empty. 3. When you finish the last question, your score will show on the screen. You pass with more than half right, so 6 or more out of 10. I expect you to look at your score and read which ones you got right. Every wrong one is a little teacher — it shows us what to practise. Mistakes are how we learn. 4. If your score is not high enough, press Try again and do the quiz one more time. This time go slower on the ones that tricked you. If you want, come and tell me which question was hard, and I will give you a hint — not the answer, a hint. 5. When your score is good, press Continue. That takes you to My progress, where you can see your ticks. You will know this page is finished when you have answered all 10 questions, seen your score, and pressed Continue to reach My progress. Ready? Start question one, and come back and tell me how it goes. 🌟

games.label: Games
games.text: Hello! Today we are on the Games page of Unit 10, My First English World. This is our fun review page. The games use words from your whole year — words like folder, favourite, proud and goal. Playing them helps those words stick in your head, ready for your capstone book and your one-minute talk. All you need is your eyes, your fingers, and your best trying voice. Here is what I expect from you: try every game, read each word out loud when you can, and use a hint when you are stuck. Mistakes are how we learn — a wrong tap just means "try again". There are three steps. Here they all are. 1. Press a game to open it, then play it. Tap one of the game cards on your screen. Read the word or look at the picture, then choose your answer. You earn stars and XP for what you know. If a question feels hard, press the hint button and take a retry — hints and retries are always there, so use them. I expect you to say each word out loud before you tap. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Play every game at least once, and play again for more stars. When one game finishes, go back and choose the next one. Do not skip any — even the ones that look tricky. If a game gave you few stars, play it one more time. The second try is nearly always better. I expect you to finish every game on the page, and to try at least one game twice. 3. When you have played them all, press I have played them all. Look over the page first and check that no game is left untouched. Then press the button called "I have played them all". If you master every single game, the page finishes by itself and you do not need the button. You will know the page is finished when it shows you as complete — either by itself after you master every game, or right after you press "I have played them all". Off you go and start with step 1. Tell me which game you picked, and how it went!

ebooks.label: Books
ebooks.text: Welcome to the Books page! This is our reading corner. Here you pick a book and read it all by yourself. We do this because reading books helps your words grow, and words are what you need for your capstone book. You need your eyes, your finger, and your reading voice. Let's start. There are three steps. 1. Choose a book from the shelf. Look at all the book covers on the screen. Look at the pictures and the titles. Pick one that makes you feel curious. Tap that book to open it. I expect you to choose with your own heart — there is no wrong book. Take your time — there's no rush. 2. Read it page by page. Press the arrow to turn to the next page. If your book plays as a video, just watch and listen. Point at the words with your finger as you read. Tap the pictures to hear their sounds — that helps you learn new words. I expect you to say the words out loud, even quietly. If a word is tricky, sound out the first letter and try again. 3. Read right to the end, then finish. Keep pressing the arrow until you reach the last page. On the last page, press Finish book. One book finishes this page. But if you loved it, read another one — reading more is always good. You will know the page is finished when you press Finish book on the last page and the page gets its tick. Then come and tell me one thing you liked in your book. Let's find out which book you choose! 📚

final-quiz.label: Final course quiz
final-quiz.text: Hello! I am your teacher for this last page. This is the Final course quiz. It is 10 questions about everything you learned this year — words, sentences, family, farm animals, senses, town places. We do it to show how much your English has grown. You do not need anything except your eyes, your thinking, and a calm, happy heart. I will not tell you any answers, but I will tell you how to think. Take your time — there's no rush. Step 1. Read the first question. Read it twice, slowly. Then look at the four choices one by one. Say each choice inside the sentence in your head and listen: does it sound right? If a question says "which word names a colour", first ask yourself, "what IS a colour?" Then find the one word that fits that group. Click the answer you think is best. I expect one careful choice for each question, not a fast guess. Step 2. Keep going the same way until all 10 questions are done. If one feels hard, that is fine — pick your best answer and move on. Mistakes are how we learn. Step 3. At the end you will see your score. Look at it and smile — every question you got right is a piece of English that is yours now. If your score is not high enough, press Try again. Do not feel sad about this. Read each question even more slowly the second time, and think about why the other choices do not fit. Step 4. When your score is good, press Continue. That is the last button of the whole course! You will know this page is finished when you have pressed Continue after a good score. Then you have finished Grade 1 English. Brilliant work! Ready? Read question one and tell me when you have chosen. I am right here.
